definition_zh: 账户；账目；账单；叙述；描述；解释；重要性
definition_en: a record of money kept with a bank or business, or a report and explanation of events
core_image: 一本摊开的账簿，每一笔进出都落在同一行上，最后合成一个交代
scene: 月底那天，店主把账本摊在柜台上，一笔一笔核对进出。At the end of the month, the shopkeeper spread the ledger on the counter and checked every account.
sceneCN: 这里 account 指账簿上的账户记录（第 1 个义项：银行或商业账户）；句意为月底店主摊开账本，逐笔核对每一个往来账户。

derivatives.zh: 由 account 加 -able 构成，义为「有责任的；须作解释的」
由 account 加 -ing 构成，义为「会计；记账」
由 account 加 -ant 构成，义为「会计员」
由 accountable 加 -ity 构成，义为「问责；责任」

senses.title: A record of money held at a bank
senses.definition: an arrangement with a bank or business that keeps a record of the money paid in and taken out
senses.definitionCN: 与银行或商号之间的安排，记录存入与取出的每一笔钱
senses.example: She opened a savings account at the branch near her office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在办公室附近的分行开了一个储蓄账户。
senses.why: The oldest bookkeeping sense: one page where money in and money out are written.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的记账义：同一页上写着进项与出项。

senses.title: A statement of money owed
senses.definition: a bill or statement showing what one party owes another
senses.definitionCN: 显示一方欠另一方多少钱的账单或结算单
senses.example: The restaurant sent the account to the company at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 餐馆在月底把账单寄给了公司。
senses.why: If one page records both sides of a deal, the same page can be sent as a claim.
senses.whyCN: 既然一页纸记下了交易的两面，这页纸也能当作索款的凭据寄出。

senses.title: A spoken or written report
senses.definition: a description of an event given by someone who saw it or took part in it
senses.definitionCN: 由目击者或参与者对事件所作的描述
senses.example: The pilot gave a calm account of the landing.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员平静地讲述了降落的过程。
senses.why: Recounting money and recounting events were once the same verb, so a story is also a telling.
senses.whyCN: 算账与讲述在过去是同一个动词，所以一段故事也是一种「交代」。

senses.title: An explanation of a cause
senses.definition: a reason or explanation that makes something understandable
senses.definitionCN: 使某件事变得可以理解的理由或说明
senses.example: No one could give an account of the sudden power failure.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能解释这次突然停电的原因。
senses.why: To account for something is to put it into the ledger of causes and make the sum balance.
senses.whyCN: 为某事作解释，就是把它记进原因的账簿，让总数轧得平。

senses.title: To explain or justify
senses.definition: to give a reason for something, especially money spent or time used
senses.definitionCN: 为某事给出理由，尤指花掉的钱或用掉的时间
senses.example: He could not account for the missing funds.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法说明那笔失踪的资金去了哪里。
senses.why: The verb keeps the bookkeeper image: every entry must answer for itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了记账人的形象：每一笔都要自己做出交代。

senses.title: To regard as
senses.definition: to consider someone or something to be a certain thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物看作某种样子
senses.example: The critics accounted the film a minor masterpiece.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家们认为这部电影是一部小小的杰作。
senses.why: Valuing is the last step of bookkeeping: what is written is finally weighed.
senses.whyCN: 估值是记账的最后一步：写下的东西最终要被称量。

intro.en: Account is a bookkeeping word that learned to tell stories, and every sense still carries a written line.
intro.cn: account 是一个学会了讲故事的记账词，每个义项里都还看得见一行字。

items.en: The verb computare meant to reckon together, built from com- (together) and putare (to reckon).
items.cn: 动词 computare 意为「合起来计算」，由 com-（共同）与 putare（估算）构成。

items.en: French turned the Latin verb into aconter, which meant both to count up and to recount events.
items.cn: 法语把那个拉丁动词变成 aconter，既指「算账」，也指「讲述事件」。

items.en: English borrowed the noun first as a reckoning of money, and soon also as a narrative.
items.cn: 英语先借入名词，指钱财的核算，很快又用来指叙述。

items.en: The commercial sense of a bank account and the verb to account for developed in this period.
items.cn: 银行账户这一商业义与动词 account for 都在这一时期发展起来。

items.en: Today the word covers money, reports, explanations, clients and value in one family.
items.cn: 今天这个词把钱财、叙述、解释、客户与重要性收在同一个词族里。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the bookkeeping family; the near-meaning group holds reports, records and bills.
note.cn: 形近组收记账词族；近义组收叙述、记录与账单一类词。

entries.definition: To reckon or add up numbers; the base of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「计数」，是这个词族的词干。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to keep and check financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计员」，专管账目。

entries.definition: The work or system of keeping financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计、记账」，指记账的工作或制度。

entries.definition: Responsible and required to explain one's actions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有责任的、须作解释的」。

entries.definition: A spoken or written description of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「报告、报道」，指对事件的描述。

entries.definition: An account of connected events, told in order.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述」，按顺序讲述一连串事件。

entries.definition: A written note kept for future reference.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记录」，留作日后查考的书面材料。

entries.definition: A statement of money owed for goods or services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账单」，列明所欠的货款或服务费。

entries.definition: A statement that makes something clear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「解释」，使事情变得清楚的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the ledger image and the phrases the word actually lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用账簿的画面，以及这个词真正栖身的短语。

normal.en: An account is a page of entries, so the word always points back to something written down.
normal.cn: account 是一页条目，所以这个词总是指回某种被写下的东西。

normal.en: Account for means to make the entries balance, that is, to explain.
normal.cn: account for 意为让账目轧平，也就是作出解释。

normal.en: On account of uses the same page as a reason: because of this entry.
normal.cn: on account of 把同一页当作理由：由于这一笔记录。

normal.en: By all accounts means judging by every report, as if every witness added a line.
normal.cn: by all accounts 意为根据各方叙述，仿佛每个证人都添了一行。

normal.en: The accountant is the person who keeps the accounts, and the suffix -ant marks the doer.
normal.cn: accountant 是记账的人，后缀 -ant 标记做事者。

abstract.en: A single ruled page where every coin leaves a dark mark.
abstract.cn: 一页画着横线的纸，每一枚硬币都留下一道深痕。

abstract.en: A shopkeeper closes the book, and the numbers inside turn into a story.
abstract.cn: 店主合上账簿，里面的数字就变成了一段故事。

abstract.en: Two columns face each other until the last line makes them equal.
abstract.cn: 两栏数字彼此对望，直到最后一行让它们相等。

examples.en: Please account for the money you spent on the trip.
examples.cn: 请说明你在旅途中花掉的钱。

examples.en: By all accounts, the concert was a great success.
examples.cn: 据大家所说，那场音乐会非常成功。

examples.en: The report gives a detailed account of the accident.
examples.cn: 这份报告对事故作了详细的叙述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额康特」——额头上记着数，一康特就把账算得清清楚楚

root: 由古法语 aconter「计算、叙述」借入，源自拉丁语 computare「合起来估算」，其中 com- 表「共同」，putare 表「估算、清点」；英语中先指钱财核算，再引申出叙述与解释义。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses follow one page of entries: money held, money owed, events told, causes explained, the act of explaining, and the weighing of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都跟着同一页账簿走：存着的钱、欠着的钱、讲述的事件、解释的缘由、解释这个动作，以及称量价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ledger line holds every sum and every story.
core.cn: 核心意象：账簿上的一行，既装着数目，也装着故事。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: money in and money out are written on one page, which can be sent as a claim.
branches.cn: 账簿线：进项与出项写在同一页，这页也能当作索款凭据寄出。

branches.en: THE STORY: the same page holds a description of what happened.
branches.cn: 叙述线：同一页也装下对发生之事的描述。

branches.en: THE REASON: a record must explain itself when questioned.
branches.cn: 解释线：一笔记录被追问时必须自我交代。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: what is written can be weighed as worth.
branches.cn: 评断线：写下的东西可以被称量为价值。

branches.en: THE PAGE: from a bank entry to a reputation, the word keeps one written line.
branches.cn: 页面线：从银行条目到名声，这个词始终保有一行字。

intro.en: The word is a Latin reckoning verb reshaped by French, and its pieces are still readable.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个被法语改造过的拉丁计算动词，构件仍然看得清。

latinIntro.en: Latin computare and putare are attested; the English noun is recorded from the thirteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 computare 与 putare 均有文献可证；英语名词自十三世纪起有记录。

items.example: It appears in account as a weakened form of ad-.
items.exampleCN: 在 account 里，它以 ad- 的弱化形式出现。

items.example: It carries the core idea of reckoning.
items.exampleCN: 它承载「核算」这一核心意思。

items.example: It joins separate sums into one total.
items.exampleCN: 它把分开的数目并成一个总数。

items.example: It is the deepest root of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个拉丁动词最深的词根。

items.example: It forms accountable from account.
items.exampleCN: 它把 account 变成 accountable。

items.example: It forms accountant, the person who keeps accounts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accountant，即记账的人。

items.example: It forms accounting, the work of keeping books.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accounting，即记账的工作。

items.example: It forms accountability from accountable.
items.exampleCN: 它由 accountable 构成 accountability。

derivatives.zh: 由 account 加 -able 构成，义为「有责任的；须作解释的」
由 account 加 -ing 构成，义为「会计；记账」
由 account 加 -ant 构成，义为「会计员」

definition_zh: 有责任的；负有解释义务的；可问责的
definition_en: required or expected to explain and answer for one's decisions and actions
core_image: 一个人站在账桌前，手指着自己签下的那一行，准备开口交代
scene: 听证会上，那位主管把文件翻到签字页，抬头看向质询的议员。At the hearing, the director turned to the page he had signed and looked up at the questioning member, ready to be accountable.
sceneCN: 这里 accountable 指须为自己的决定作出交代（第 1 个义项：对决定负责）；句意为主管翻到自己签字的那一页，准备接受质询。

pos.zh: 有责任的；须作解释的；可问责的

derivatives.zh: 由 accountable 加 -ity 构成，义为「问责；责任」
由 accountable 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「无需负责的；无法解释的」
由 accountable 加 -ly 构成，义为「负责任地」

senses.title: Responsible for one's decisions
senses.definition: expected to answer for choices one has made and their results
senses.definitionCN: 须为自己所作的抉择及其结果作出交代
senses.example: Managers are accountable for the targets they set.
senses.exampleCN: 经理们要为自己设定的目标负责。
senses.why: To be accountable is to be the person whose name stands beside the entry.
senses.whyCN: 有责任，就是成为名字写在那一笔记录旁边的人。

senses.title: Required to explain
senses.definition: obliged to give an explanation when asked
senses.definitionCN: 在被问询时有义务给出说明
senses.example: The officer was accountable to the committee for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 那名官员须就延误向委员会作出解释。
senses.why: The ledger sense survives: the entry must speak when the book is opened.
senses.whyCN: 账簿义仍在：翻开本子时，那一笔必须开口说话。

senses.title: Answerable to an authority
senses.definition: under the authority of a person or body that can question one
senses.definitionCN: 处于某人或某机构的管辖之下，须接受其质询
senses.example: The agency is accountable to the ministry that funds it.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构对提供资金的部委负责。
senses.why: A line in a book always belongs to a higher account that checks it.
senses.whyCN: 账簿里的一行总归属于更高一级的账，由后者来核对。

senses.title: Open to public scrutiny
senses.definition: operating in a way that allows others to examine and judge
senses.definitionCN: 以允许他人查看与评判的方式运作
senses.example: Elections are meant to make officials accountable.
senses.exampleCN: 选举的意义在于让官员接受问责。
senses.why: Open books can be audited, and open power can be questioned.
senses.whyCN: 账本摊开才能被审计，权力摊开才能被质询。

intro.en: Accountable is account plus able, and it names the person who must answer for the page.
intro.cn: accountable 是 account 加 -able，命名的是那个必须为这一页作出交代的人。

items.en: The reckoning verb computare is the distant source of the whole family.
items.cn: 计算动词 computare 是整个词族遥远的源头。

items.en: French aconter carried the twin ideas of counting and recounting.
items.cn: 法语 aconter 兼有「算账」与「讲述」两层意思。

items.en: English account first meant a reckoning, then a report that must be given.
items.cn: 英语 account 先指核算，再指必须交出的报告。

items.en: The ending able turned the noun into an adjective of obligation.
items.cn: 词尾 able 把名词变成带义务意味的形容词。

items.en: Today the word is at home in law, politics and public administration.
items.cn: 今天这个词活跃在法律、政治与公共管理之中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the account family; the near-meaning group is the vocabulary of responsibility.
note.cn: 形近组是 account 词族；近义组是表示责任的词。

entries.definition: A record of money, or a report of events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「账户、账目」或「叙述」。

entries.definition: The obligation to explain and accept responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「问责、责任」，指作出交代的义务。

entries.definition: A person who keeps and inspects financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计员」，负责记账与查账。

entries.definition: The practice of keeping financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计」，指记账的实务。

entries.definition: Having a duty to deal with something and answer for it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负责的」，对某事负有处理与交代之责。

entries.definition: Required to explain or justify one's actions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「须作出解释的」，最贴近本词。

entries.definition: Legally responsible for payment or damage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有法律责任的」，多用于赔偿。

entries.definition: Open to being controlled or judged by a higher body.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「愿受管辖的、可被问责的」，较正式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks attach the adjective to the ledger and to the preposition that usually follows it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个形容词拴在账簿上，也拴在它常跟的介词上。

normal.en: Account plus able: able to give an account when asked.
normal.cn: account 加 able：被问到时能够交出一份账。

normal.en: The usual frame is accountable for a deed and accountable to a person.
normal.cn: 常见框架是 accountable for 对某件事负责，accountable to 对某人负责。

normal.en: Hold someone accountable means put the open book in front of them.
normal.cn: hold someone accountable 就是把摊开的账本摆到某人面前。

normal.en: The noun accountability is the state; the adjective describes the person in that state.
normal.cn: 名词 accountability 指这种状态，形容词则形容处于该状态的人。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with accounting, which is the work, not the duty.
normal.cn: 不要与 accounting 混淆，后者是记账的工作，不是责任。

abstract.en: A name written at the bottom of a page, waiting to be asked about the line above it.
abstract.cn: 一个名字写在页脚，等着有人来问上面那一行。

abstract.en: A hand raised in a meeting before the question has finished.
abstract.cn: 会议上一只手在问题还没问完时就举了起来。

abstract.en: A key left in the lock of an open ledger, so anyone may turn it.
abstract.cn: 一把钥匙留在摊开账簿的锁孔里，谁都能转动。

examples.en: Ministers are accountable to Parliament for their decisions.
examples.cn: 大臣们要为自己的决定向议会负责。

examples.en: No one was held accountable for the error.
examples.cn: 没有人因这个错误被追究责任。

examples.en: The system makes every officer accountable for the money spent.
examples.cn: 这套制度让每位官员对所花的钱负责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额康特波」——额头上记着账，康特一拨就有人站出来认账

root: 由 account 加形容词后缀 -able 构成；account 来自古法语 aconter，再上溯拉丁语 computare「合起来估算」；-able 最初表「可被……的」，加在记账名词上便生出「须作交代、须负责」之义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses hold one duty: answering for a decision, explaining it when asked, answering to an authority, and facing public scrutiny.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项守着一份义务：为决定负责、被问时作出解释、向上级交代，以及接受公众监督。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed line in a ledger, and the signer must speak for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：账簿上一行签字，签字人必须为它开口。

branches.en: THE DECISION: the signer answers for the choice made.
branches.cn: 决定线：签字人为所作的抉择负责。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION: the entry must speak when the book is opened.
branches.cn: 解释说线：翻开本子时，那一笔必须开口。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: a higher account always checks the lower one.
branches.cn: 上级线：更高的账总要核对更低的那一本。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC: open books can be audited, and open power can be questioned.
branches.cn: 监督线：账本摊开可审计，权力公开可质询。

branches.en: THE SIGNATURE: responsibility begins with a name and a reason.
branches.cn: 签名线：责任从一个名字和一条理由开始。

intro.en: Three pieces carry the whole idea: the account, the ability, and the obligation.
intro.cn: 三个构件撑起整个意思：账、能力与义务。

latinIntro.en: The Latin reckoning verb computare and the suffix -abilis both survive in this adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁计算动词 computare 与后缀 -abilis 都活在这个形容词里。

items.example: It supplies the page that must be answered for.
items.exampleCN: 它提供那一页需要被交代的账。

items.example: It turns the noun into a duty.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成一份义务。

items.example: It forms accountability from this adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它由这个形容词构成 accountability。

items.example: It is the weakened ad- inside account.
items.exampleCN: 它是 account 里弱化了的 ad-。

items.example: It makes the reckoning a joint sum.
items.exampleCN: 它让核算成为一个合起来的数。

items.example: It is the root of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个拉丁动词的词根。

items.example: It forms unaccountable, meaning not required to answer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unaccountable，意为「无需作出交代的」。

items.example: It forms accountably, meaning in a responsible way.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accountably，意为「负责任地」。

derivatives.zh: 由 accountable 加 -ity 构成，义为「问责；责任」
由 accountable 加 un- 构成，义为「无需负责的；无法解释的」

definition_zh: 积累；积聚；堆积；攒下；逐渐增多
definition_en: to gather or increase gradually over a period of time
core_image: 谷仓角落的一小堆谷物，一把一把添上去，最后高过门槛
scene: 老农每天把晒干的谷子扫进仓角，从不一次倒完。Every day the old farmer swept the dried grain into the corner of the barn, and by winter it had accumulated past the threshold.
sceneCN: 这里 accumulated 指谷物一点点堆高（第 3 个义项：物质堆积）；句意为老农每天扫进一点，到冬天已堆得高过门槛。

derivatives.zh: 由 accumulate 加 -ion 构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由 accumulate 加 -ive 构成，义为「累积性的」
由 accumulate 加 -or 构成，义为「积累者；蓄电池」

senses.title: To gather more and more over time
senses.definition: to collect or gain things gradually, so that the total keeps growing
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐收集或获得，使总量不断增加
senses.example: She accumulated a large library over thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 三十年间她积累了满满一屋藏书。
senses.why: A heap grows one shovelful at a time, and the verb keeps that patient rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 土堆是一铲一铲长起来的，这个动词保留着那种缓慢的节奏。

senses.title: To increase gradually in quantity
senses.definition: to become greater in amount without any single large addition
senses.definitionCN: 在没有任何一次大量增加的情况下数量逐渐变大
senses.example: Debt can accumulate quietly for years.
senses.exampleCN: 债务可以悄无声息地累积多年。
senses.why: Nothing is added at once, yet the heap at the corner keeps rising.
senses.whyCN: 没有一次添加很多，可角落的堆却一直在升高。

senses.title: To pile up physically
senses.definition: to form a heap of material, as snow, dust or grain
senses.definitionCN: 形成一堆物质，如雪、灰尘或谷物
senses.example: Snow accumulated against the northern wall.
senses.exampleCN: 雪在朝北的墙边堆积起来。
senses.why: The Latin word for heap is cumulus, and the verb literally means to heap up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里「堆」是 cumulus，这个动词字面就是「堆起来」。

senses.title: To save money or goods
senses.definition: to put money or supplies aside until a useful amount is reached
senses.definitionCN: 把钱或物资留存起来，直到达到可用的数量
senses.example: They accumulated enough grain to last the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们攒下了足够过冬的粮食。
senses.why: Saving is the domestic form of heaping: small amounts, kept in one place.
senses.whyCN: 储蓄是堆积的家庭版本：少量多次，都放在同一处。

senses.title: To build up arrears or debt
senses.definition: to let unpaid amounts add up, often through neglect
senses.definitionCN: 让未付的款项不断叠加，常因疏忽而起
senses.example: Unpaid rent accumulated while he was away.
senses.exampleCN: 他外出期间，未付的房租越积越多。
senses.why: The same heap can be made of obligations instead of grain.
senses.whyCN: 同一个堆，也可以由欠下的义务堆成，而不是谷物。

senses.title: To collect evidence or knowledge
senses.definition: to bring together facts, data or learning piece by piece
senses.definitionCN: 一点一点地把事实、数据或学问汇集起来
senses.example: The team accumulated data for three years before publishing.
senses.exampleCN: 团队收集了三年数据才发表成果。
senses.why: Knowledge behaves like grain: no single grain matters, the heap does.
senses.whyCN: 知识像谷物：单单一粒不重要，重要的是那一堆。

intro.en: Accumulate is Latin ad plus cumulus, to heap toward, and every sense keeps the shape of a growing pile.
intro.cn: accumulate 是拉丁语 ad 加 cumulus，意为「堆向一处」，每个义项都保留着一堆东西长高的形状。

items.en: Cumulus meant a heap or a pile, and it still names a heap-shaped cloud.
items.cn: cumulus 意为「堆、垛」，今天仍用来命名堆状的云。

items.en: The verb accumulare meant to heap up, built with the prefix ad-, toward.
items.cn: 动词 accumulare 意为「堆起来」，由表示「朝向」的前缀 ad- 构成。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century, first in the physical sense of heaping.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，最初是「堆积」的实义。

items.en: The financial sense of interest and savings adding up appeared in this period.
items.cn: 利息与储蓄叠加的财务义在这一时期出现。

items.en: Today the word serves for snow, debt, data, wealth and grudges alike.
items.cn: 今天这个词同时用于积雪、债务、数据、财富与怨气。

note.en: The look-alike group is the cumulus family; the near-meaning group is the verbs of gathering.
note.cn: 形近组是 cumulus 词族；近义组是表示聚集的动词。

entries.definition: The process or result of heaping things up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「积累、堆积物」，指堆积的过程或结果。

entries.definition: Tending to grow by repeated additions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「累积性的」，靠一再添加而增长。

entries.definition: A heap-shaped cloud, and the Latin word for a heap.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「积云」，也是拉丁语里的「堆」。

entries.definition: Increasing by successive additions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「累积的」，靠接连相加而增加。

entries.definition: To bring things together from different places.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收集」，把各处的东西聚到一起。

entries.definition: To gather a large amount, especially wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积聚」，尤指积攒大量财富。

entries.definition: To put things in a heap, one on another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「堆放」，把东西一层层叠起来。

entries.definition: To store a large supply for future use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「囤积」，为将来储备大量物资。

entries.definition: To come or bring together in one place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「聚集」，聚拢到一处。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin heap and the many things that can pile up.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用拉丁语「堆」的画面，以及各种能堆起来的东西。

normal.en: Cumulus is a heap, so accumulate means to heap toward oneself.
normal.cn: cumulus 是「堆」，所以 accumulate 就是往自己这边堆。

normal.en: The noun is accumulation, and the cloud cumulus keeps the same shape.
normal.cn: 名词是 accumulation，而云名 cumulus 保留着同样的形状。

normal.en: Interest accumulates, debt accumulates, snow accumulates: all grow by small additions.
normal.cn: 利息会积，债务会积，雪会积：都靠一次次小量添加。

normal.en: Use accumulate for things that grow slowly, not for a single large purchase.
normal.cn: accumulate 用于缓慢增长的事物，不用于一次大量买进。

normal.en: Accumulated experience is the heap that makes an expert.
normal.cn: 积累的经验就是堆成专家的那一堆东西。

abstract.en: A shovel lifts one spadeful and adds it to a pile that never stops rising.
abstract.cn: 一把铲子铲起一铲，添到一堆始终在长高的东西上。

abstract.en: Coins dropped into a jar one at a time until the lid will not close.
abstract.cn: 硬币一枚枚丢进罐子，直到盖子合不上。

abstract.en: A corner of a room where dust gathers while nobody looks.
abstract.cn: 房间一角，没人注意时灰尘自己积了起来。

examples.en: Dust accumulated on the shelves while the house was empty.
examples.cn: 房子空着的时候，架子上积了灰。

examples.en: He accumulated enough capital to open a second shop.
examples.cn: 他攒够了资金，开了第二家店。

examples.en: Small errors accumulate into serious problems.
examples.cn: 小错误累积起来就成了严重问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额Q缪累特」——额头上那个Q，缪缪地累成一堆特高的东西

root: 源自拉丁语 accumulare「堆起来」，由 ad-（朝向）加 cumulus（堆、垛）构成；cumulus 至今仍指堆状的积云，词根义「堆高」贯穿全部义项。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses describe one rising total: things, savings, debts, data and knowledge, each growing by small additions.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项描述同一个不断升高的总量：物品、存款、债务、数据与知识，都靠一次次小量添加。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap that grows one shovelful at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆东西，一铲一铲地长高。

branches.en: THE HEAP: small additions make a large total without any single big event.
branches.cn: 堆高线：一次次小添加，没有任何大动作，却成了大总量。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: snow, dust and grain obey the same physical law.
branches.cn: 物料线：雪、灰尘与谷物服从同一条物理规律。

branches.en: THE SAVING: money kept aside becomes a heap.
branches.cn: 储蓄线：留起来的钱堆成一垛。

branches.en: THE DEBT: obligations pile up when nothing is paid.
branches.cn: 债务线：什么都不付时，义务也会堆起来。

branches.en: THE RECORD: evidence and knowledge grow where no one is watching.
branches.cn: 记录线：证据与知识在无人看见处增长。

intro.en: The verb is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin noun that still names a cloud.
intro.cn: 这个动词由一个拉丁前缀和一个至今仍命名云朵的拉丁名词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cumulus and accumulare are attested; the English verb is recorded from the fifteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cumulus 与 accumulare 均有文献可证；英语动词自十五世纪起有记录。

items.example: It directs the heaping toward one place.
items.exampleCN: 它把堆积的方向指向一处。

items.example: It gives the word its shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给了这个词「堆」的形状。

items.example: It forms the verb from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成动词。

items.example: It forms accumulation from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成 accumulation。

items.example: It forms accumulative.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accumulative。

items.example: It forms accumulator, also a kind of battery.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accumulator，也指一种蓄电池。

items.example: It appears in cumulonimbus, the towering cloud.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 cumulonimbus，即高耸的积雨云。

items.example: It forms accumulated, meaning heaped up.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accumulated，意为「已堆积的」。

derivatives.zh: 由 accumulate 加 -ion 构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由 accumulate 加 -ive 构成，义为「累积性的」
由 accumulate 加 -or 构成，义为「积累者；蓄电池」

definition_zh: 准确的；精确的；精准的；忠实于原貌的
definition_en: correct in every detail and free from error
core_image: 一把卡尺卡住零件边缘，两个刻度的读数严丝合缝
scene: 测绘队在雨里把同一条边复测了三遍，每一个数字都要对得上。The survey team measured the same line three times in the rain so that every figure would be accurate.
sceneCN: 这里 accurate 指测量结果精确无误（第 2 个义项：度量精确）；句意为测绘队反复测量，务求每个数字都对得上。

derivatives.zh: 由 accurate 加 -cy 构成，义为「准确；精确度」
由 accurate 加 -ly 构成，义为「准确地」
由 accurate 加 -ness 构成，义为「准确的性质」

senses.title: Correct in every detail
senses.definition: giving all details correctly, with nothing added or left out
senses.definitionCN: 细节全都正确，既无添补也无遗漏
senses.example: Her description of the room was accurate in every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个房间的描述每个细节都准确。
senses.why: The Latin word for care grew into a word for doing something with full care.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里「用心」这个词，长成了「事事用心做到」的意思。

senses.title: Exact in measurement
senses.definition: measured or calculated with a very small margin of error
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算时误差极小的
senses.example: The instrument is accurate to a tenth of a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器的精度达到十分之一度。
senses.why: A careful hand makes a tight measurement, and the word keeps that tightness.
senses.whyCN: 手足够仔细，量出的数才收得紧，这个词保留了那份紧。

senses.title: Hitting the target
senses.definition: of a throw or shot, arriving exactly where it was aimed
senses.definitionCN: 指投掷或射击正好落在瞄准的位置
senses.example: His first shot was accurate from forty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 他第一枪在四十米外就精准命中。
senses.why: Care in the hand shows up as the arrow in the centre of the ring.
senses.whyCN: 手上的用心，最后显示为箭插在靶心。

senses.title: Faithful to the original
senses.definition: of a copy or translation, matching the source without distortion
senses.definitionCN: 指复制或翻译与原文相符，不走样
senses.example: The translation is accurate but a little stiff.
senses.exampleCN: 这份译文准确，只是略嫌生硬。
senses.why: Accuracy is care turned toward another text rather than toward a target.
senses.whyCN: 准确在这里是把用心朝向另一份文本，而不是朝向靶子。

intro.en: Accurate comes from Latin care, and its whole history is about doing something with enough care to be right.
intro.cn: accurate 出自拉丁语的「用心」，整段历史都关于把一件事做得足够用心、因而正确。

items.en: Cura meant care, concern and attentive treatment.
items.cn: cura 意为「用心、关切、仔细照料」。

items.en: The verb accurare, built with ad-, meant to give careful attention to something.
items.cn: 动词 accurare 由 ad- 构成，意为「对某事悉心处理」。

items.en: Its participle accuratus meant done with care, and so exact.
items.cn: 它的分词 accuratus 意为「用心做成的」，因而「精确的」。

items.en: English took the participle directly from Latin as an adjective of precision.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入这个分词，用作表示精确的形容词。

items.en: Today the word covers figures, shots, translations, instruments and forecasts.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖数字、射击、翻译、仪器与预报。

note.en: The look-alike group is the cura family; the near-meaning group is the adjectives of exactness.
note.cn: 形近组是 cura 词族；近义组是表示精确的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being correct and exact.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准确、精确度」。

entries.definition: In a correct and exact way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「准确地」。

entries.definition: The state of being free from error.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准确无误的状态」，较少用。

entries.definition: Eager to know, from the same Latin root meaning care.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好奇的」，与本源共享「用心」这一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: Stated or measured with great exactness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精确的」，强调细节分毫分明。

entries.definition: Correct in every particular, with nothing approximate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「确切的」，没有任何约略。

entries.definition: Free from error, agreeing with the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正确的」，与事实相符。

entries.definition: Of a copy, matching the original closely.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「忠实的」，指复制品贴近原貌。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin idea of care and the fields where the word is used.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用拉丁语「用心」的意思，以及这个词出没的场合。

normal.en: The root is cura, care: what is done with care comes out accurate.
normal.cn: 词根是 cura「用心」：用心做出来的东西才准确。

normal.en: The noun is accuracy, the adverb accurately, and the adjective keeps the final ate.
normal.cn: 名词是 accuracy，副词是 accurately，形容词保留词尾 ate。

normal.en: Accurate goes with figures, clocks, scales, maps and forecasts.
normal.cn: accurate 常与数字、钟表、天平、地图和预报搭配。

normal.en: Say accurate about a result, not accurate for a person's effort.
normal.cn: 说结果 accurate，不说某人的努力 accurate。

normal.en: Precise stresses fine detail; accurate stresses freedom from error.
normal.cn: precise 强调细节精细，accurate 强调没有错误。

abstract.en: A caliper closes on a metal edge until the two marks line up exactly.
abstract.cn: 卡尺合上金属边缘，两个刻度正好对齐。

abstract.en: An arrow stands in the very centre of the target, not near it.
abstract.cn: 箭插在靶的正中心，而不是旁边。

abstract.en: A hand steadies a ruler so that the pencil follows the line without wavering.
abstract.cn: 一只手稳稳按住尺子，铅笔沿着线走，毫不偏移。

examples.en: The map is accurate enough for walkers to follow.
examples.cn: 这张地图足够准确，步行者可以照着走。

examples.en: We need accurate figures before we set the budget.
examples.cn: 定预算之前我们需要准确的数字。

examples.en: His account of the meeting was accurate in every detail.
examples.cn: 他对会议的叙述每个细节都准确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱Q瑞特」——爱较真的人拿Q去量，瑞特一下，分毫都不差

root: 源自拉丁语 accuratus，是 accurare「悉心处理」的分词，由 ad-（朝向）加 cura（用心、照料）构成；词根 cura 义为「用心」，用心到位则结果精确。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses share one condition, freedom from error, in details, in measurement, in a shot, and in a copy.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共享同一个条件——没有错误，分别落在细节、测量、射击与复制上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two marks meeting exactly, with no gap and no overlap.
core.cn: 核心意象：两道刻度正好对齐，不留缝也不重叠。

branches.en: THE DETAIL: every particular is right.
branches.cn: 细节线：每一个细节都对。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a careful instrument gives a tight reading.
branches.cn: 度量线：用心的仪器给出收得很紧的读数。

branches.en: THE TARGET: care in the hand ends as a hit in the centre.
branches.cn: 靶心线：手上的用心最后落在正中心。

branches.en: THE COPY: faithfulness is accuracy pointed at another text.
branches.cn: 复制线：忠实就是把准确对准另一份文本。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: a report and a translation are both judged against an original.
branches.cn: 真实线：报告与译文都要对着一个原本受检。

intro.en: One Latin root, care, plus a participle ending, and the word is complete.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁词根「用心」，加一个分词词尾，这个词就完整了。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura and accurare are well attested; the English adjective appears in the seventeenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 与 accurare 均有充分文献可证；英语形容词出现于十七世纪。

items.example: It is the deepest root of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词最深的词根。

items.example: It points the care at something.
items.exampleCN: 它把用心指向某个对象。

items.example: It marks the word as a finished state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记这个词是一种已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms accuracy from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它由形容词构成 accuracy。

items.example: It forms accurately.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accurately。

items.example: It forms accurateness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accurateness。

items.example: It keeps the same root but shifts care into wanting to know.
items.exampleCN: 它保留同一词根，却把「用心」转向「想知道」。

items.meaning: to take care of a sick person
items.example: It comes from the same Latin noun for care.
items.exampleCN: 它出自同一个表示「照料」的拉丁名词。

latinEntries.meaning: to take care of, to prepare carefully

definition_zh: 指控；控告；指责；罪名；被指摘的过错
definition_en: a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal
core_image: 一个人伸出手指，直直指向对面那人的胸口
scene: 会议室里，两份报告被推到桌子中央，一方的代表站起来指向对面。In the meeting room two reports were pushed to the centre of the table, and one delegate stood up and made an accusation.
sceneCN: 这里 accusation 指一方对另一方提出的指控（第 1 个义项：指称对方做错事）；句意为两份报告摆到桌中，一方代表起身指控。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「指控；指责」
由 accuse 加 -er 构成，义为「指控者；原告」
由 accuse 加 -atory 构成，义为「指责的；控告的」
由 accuse 加 -ed 构成，义为「被告；被指控的」

senses.title: A claim that someone did wrong
senses.definition: a statement that a person has done something wrong, made without proof yet
senses.definitionCN: 指称某人做错了事，且此时尚无证据的说法
senses.example: His accusation surprised everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他的指控让桌旁所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bring a case against someone, and a case begins with a claim.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「对某人立案」，而案子总是从一句指称开始。

senses.title: A formal legal charge
senses.definition: a charge brought officially against a person in a court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上对某人正式提出的控诉
senses.example: The accusation was read out before the judge.
senses.exampleCN: 控告在法官面前被宣读。
senses.why: A court charge is that claim written down and made official.
senses.whyCN: 法庭上的控告，就是把那句指称写下来并盖上官方印记。

senses.title: The act of accusing
senses.definition: the action of pointing out someone's fault, rather than the words used
senses.definitionCN: 指出他人过错这一动作，而不是指所用的言辞
senses.example: His accusation came before any evidence was heard.
senses.exampleCN: 他的指责在听取任何证据之前就来了。
senses.why: The noun can name either the sentence spoken or the act of speaking it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既可是说出的那句话，也可是说话这个动作。

senses.title: A fault one is blamed for
senses.definition: the wrongdoing itself, seen as something laid at a person's door
senses.definitionCN: 指那件过错本身，被视为放在某人门口的东西
senses.example: The accusation against the clerk was carelessness.
senses.exampleCN: 对那名职员的指摘是粗心大意。
senses.why: What is charged can be summed up in a single word, such as neglect.
senses.whyCN: 被指控的事往往能用一个词概括，比如疏忽。

intro.en: Accusation is the noun of a Latin law term, and it still smells of the courtroom.
intro.cn: accusation 是一个拉丁法律术语的名词形式，至今仍带法庭的气息。

items.en: Causa meant a cause, a reason, and also a lawsuit.
items.cn: causa 意为「原因、理由」，也指「诉讼案件」。

items.en: Accusare meant to call someone to account, to bring a charge.
items.cn: accusare 意为「传某人来交代」，即提出控告。

items.en: The noun accusatio named the charge itself and the act of bringing it.
items.cn: 名词 accusatio 既指罪名本身，也指提出控告的行为。

items.en: French carried the noun into legal and everyday use.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入法律与日常使用。

items.en: English borrowed it for both the legal charge and the everyday blame.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，既指法律控告，也指日常指责。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accuse family; the near-meaning group is the vocabulary of formal charges.
note.cn: 形近组是 accuse 词族；近义组是表示正式控诉的词。

entries.definition: The person charged in a criminal case.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被告」，指刑事案件中被控的一方。

entries.definition: The person who brings a charge.

entries.definition: Showing that one blames another person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「指责的、控告的」。

entries.definition: A formal statement that someone has committed a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指控、罪名」，多为法律用语。

entries.definition: A claim of wrongdoing that has not been proved.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指称」，强调尚未证实。

entries.definition: A formal accusation issued by a grand jury.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正式起诉」，多用于英美法系。

entries.definition: A statement that something is wrong or unsatisfactory.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投诉、抱怨」，语气最轻。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the pointing finger and the legal phrases the noun keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子顺着那根指着人的手指，以及这个名词保留的法律短语。

normal.en: The verb is accuse, the noun is accusation, and the person is the accuser.
normal.cn: 动词是 accuse，名词是 accusation，提出指控的人是 accuser。

normal.en: The usual frame is an accusation of something against someone.
normal.cn: 常见框架是 an accusation of 某事 against 某人。

normal.en: A false accusation is the worst kind, because the gesture is right and the cause is empty.
normal.cn: 诬告最坏，因为动作没错，理由却是空的。

normal.en: Level an accusation means aim it, as a weapon is levelled at a mark.
normal.cn: level an accusation 意为把指控对准目标，像把武器平举瞄准。

normal.en: In law the word is formal; in daily talk it often means plain blame.
normal.cn: 在法律里这个词很正式，在日常话里常只表示责怪。

abstract.en: A finger held steady in the air while the room falls silent.
abstract.cn: 一根手指稳稳举在空中，房间里安静下来。

abstract.en: A name written on a charge sheet and read aloud.
abstract.cn: 一个名字写在控罪书上，被大声念出。

abstract.en: Two hands pointing at each other across a table.
abstract.cn: 两只手隔着桌子指向对方。

examples.en: She denied the accusation at once.
examples.cn: 她立刻否认了这项指控。

examples.en: The accusation was based on rumour rather than evidence.
examples.cn: 这项指控依据的是传闻而非证据。

examples.en: He faced an accusation of taking bribes.
examples.cn: 他面临收受贿赂的指控。

root: 来自拉丁语 accusatio，源自动词 accusare「提出控告」，由 ad-（朝向）加 causa（原因、诉讼案件）构成；古法语作 accusation，英语十四世纪借入，兼指法律控告与日常指责。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses cover the claim itself, the legal charge, the act of accusing, and the fault one is blamed for.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项覆盖指称本身、法律控告、指责这个动作，以及被指摘的过错。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointed straight at another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指直直指向另一个人。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: the words spoken and the act of speaking them both carry this name.
branches.cn: 指称线：说出的那句话与说话的动作，都叫这个名字。

branches.en: THE COURT: a charge is that claim written down and made official.
branches.cn: 法庭线：控告就是那句指称被写下并盖上官方印记。

branches.en: THE FAULT: what is charged can usually be summed up in one word.
branches.cn: 过错线：被指控的事往往能用一个词概括。

branches.en: THE FINGER: a claim and a fault meet at the tip of one pointing gesture.
branches.cn: 手指线：指称与过错，在同一个指人的动作尖端相遇。

branches.en: THE RECORD: the act of accusing is what turns a claim into a case.
branches.cn: 案卷线：正是指责这个动作，把一句指称变成一桩案子。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction, a Latin noun of cause, and two noun endings built the word.
intro.cn: 一个表示方向的拉丁前缀、一个表示原因与诉讼的拉丁名词，加两个名词词尾，拼成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin causa and accusare are attested; the English noun appears in the fourteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 causa 与 accusare 均有文献可证；英语名词出现于十四世纪。

items.example: It turns the charge toward a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把指控的方向指向某人。

items.example: It joins reason and legal case in one word.
items.exampleCN: 它把理由与法律案件合在一个词里。

items.example: It forms the verb accusare.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词 accusare。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成名词。

items.example: It forms accuser.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accuser。

items.example: It forms the noun accused, the person charged.
items.exampleCN: 它构成名词 accused，即被告。

items.example: It forms accusatory.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accusatory。

items.meaning: reason, or a principle one supports
items.example: It descends from the same Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 它出自同一个拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 指控；指责；控告；归咎
definition_en: to say that someone has done something wrong, dishonest or illegal
core_image: 一句话像一根手指，越过桌面直接点到某个人身上
scene: 法官敲了敲桌面，检察官转向被告席，开始说明起诉的理由。The judge tapped the desk, and the prosecutor turned to the dock and began to accuse the man of fraud.
sceneCN: 这里 accuse 指检察官当庭指控被告（第 2 个义项：正式控告）；句意为法官敲桌，检察官转向被告席开始指控其诈骗。

由 accuse 加 -er 构成，义为「指控者；原告」

由 accuse 加 -atory 构成，义为「指责的」

senses.title: To say someone did wrong
senses.definition: to state that a person has done something bad, without yet proving it
senses.definitionCN: 指称某人做了不好的事，尚未加以证明
senses.example: She accused him of ignoring her messages.
senses.exampleCN: 她指责他不回她的消息。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bring a case, and a case opens with a claim.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「立案」，而案子从一句指称开始。

senses.title: To charge formally
senses.definition: to bring an official charge against someone in a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上对某人正式提出控诉
senses.example: The company was accused of tax evasion.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被控逃税。
senses.why: The courtroom is where the pointing finger is written down as a charge.
senses.whyCN: 法庭正是那根指人的手指被写成控罪的地方。

senses.title: To blame for a fault
senses.definition: to hold someone answerable for a mistake or misfortune
senses.definitionCN: 要某人为错误或不幸承担责任
senses.example: They accused the weather for the poor harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把歉收归咎于天气。
senses.why: If a fault must land on someone, the finger will find a target.
senses.whyCN: 过错总要落到某人头上，手指就会找到目标。

senses.title: To allege a crime
senses.definition: to claim that a specific offence was committed by a specific person
senses.definitionCN: 声称某项具体罪行是某个具体的人犯下的
senses.example: He was accused of stealing the files.
senses.exampleCN: 他被指控偷走了那些文件。
senses.why: A specific offence turns a general complaint into a charge with edges.
senses.whyCN: 一项具体罪行，把泛泛的抱怨变成了有棱有角的控罪。

senses.title: To criticize sharply
senses.definition: to attack a policy or group in strong words
senses.definitionCN: 用严厉的言辞攻击某项政策或某个群体
senses.example: The report accuses the ministry of moving too slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 报告抨击该部委行动迟缓。
senses.why: Public criticism is the same gesture performed at a larger target.
senses.whyCN: 公开批评是同一个动作，只是指向更大的目标。

intro.en: Accuse is a law word from Latin, and it has kept the shape of a charge laid against a person.
intro.cn: accuse 是一个来自拉丁语的法律词，一直保留着「对某人立案」的形状。

items.en: Causa covered a cause, a reason and a lawsuit.
items.cn: causa 兼指原因、理由与诉讼案件。

items.en: Accusare meant to call a person to account before a court.
items.cn: accusare 意为「传某人到法庭交代」。

items.en: French shortened the verb to acuser and kept its legal force.
items.cn: 法语把它缩成 acuser，保留了法律上的力度。

items.en: English took the verb in the thirteenth century, first in legal texts.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个动词，最早见于法律文本。

items.en: The word now covers court charges, public criticism and everyday blame.
items.cn: 今天这个词涵盖法庭控告、公开抨击与日常责怪。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accusation family; the near-meaning group is the verbs of charging and blaming.
note.cn: 形近组是 accusation 词族；近义组是表示控告与责怪的动词。

entries.definition: A claim or charge that someone did wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指控、罪名」。

entries.definition: A person who brings a charge against another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指控者、原告」。

entries.definition: The person against whom a charge is brought.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被告」。

entries.definition: Expressing blame or a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「指责的、控告的」。

entries.definition: To formally state that someone has committed an offence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「控告、起诉」，法律色彩最重。

entries.definition: To say or think that someone is responsible for something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「责怪」，侧重认定责任。

entries.definition: To formally charge someone with a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「正式起诉」，多由大陪审团作出。

entries.definition: To state that something is true without proof yet.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「指称」，强调尚未证实。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fixed preposition of and the courtroom image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用固定的介词 of，以及法庭的画面。

normal.en: Accuse takes of before the fault: accuse someone of theft.
normal.cn: accuse 后面用 of 引出过错：accuse someone of theft。

normal.en: The noun is accusation, the person charging is the accuser, the person charged is the accused.
normal.cn: 名词是 accusation，指控者是 accuser，被指控者是 accused。

normal.en: In law one is accused of a crime; in daily life one is accused of a habit or a slight.
normal.cn: 法律上被指控的是罪行；日常里被指责的是习惯或小过失。

normal.en: Stand accused of is a formal phrase used in news reports.
normal.cn: stand accused of 是新闻中常见的正式说法。

normal.en: Do not say accuse for; the fault is named with of.
normal.cn: 不要说 accuse for，过错要用 of 引出。

abstract.en: A finger crosses the table and stops an inch from a chest.
abstract.cn: 一根手指越过桌面，停在离胸口一寸的地方。

abstract.en: A clerk writes a name at the top of a charge sheet.
abstract.cn: 一名书记员把名字写在控罪书的最上方。

abstract.en: A single word spoken loudly in a quiet hall.
abstract.cn: 安静的大厅里，一个词被说得格外响。

examples.en: They accused him of breaking the agreement.
examples.cn: 他们指控他违反了协议。

examples.en: The report accuses several firms of hiding losses.
examples.cn: 报告指控数家公司隐瞒亏损。

examples.en: He was accused of careless work, not of dishonesty.
examples.cn: 他被指责工作粗心，而不是不诚实。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses speak a charge: in daily blame, in court, in attributing a fault, in naming a crime, and in public criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都是把一句控诉说出来：日常责怪、法庭控告、归咎、指明罪名，以及公开抨击。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sentence shaped like a finger, aimed at a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句像手指的话，对准某个人。

branches.en: THE CLAIM AND THE BLAME: the same words serve a quarrel or a misfortune.
branches.cn: 指称与责怪线：同一句话既可用于争吵，也可用于不幸。

branches.en: THE COURT: the finger becomes a written charge.
branches.cn: 法庭线：手指变成一纸控罪。

branches.en: THE OFFENCE: a specific crime gives the claim a name.
branches.cn: 罪行线：一项具体罪名让指称有了名字。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC VOICE: criticism is the gesture performed at scale.
branches.cn: 公开线：批评是把同一动作放大来做。

branches.en: THE FINGER: from a private complaint to a public attack, the shape never changes.
branches.cn: 手指线：从私下抱怨到公开攻击，形状始终不变。

definition_zh: 使习惯；使适应；使身体耐受
definition_en: to make someone or oneself used to something through repeated experience
core_image: 同一件事被重复到第十遍，人的身体先于头脑不再抗拒
scene: 驯犬师每天早上带幼犬走过喧闹的市场，让它在人群里保持安静。Every morning the trainer accustoms the young dog to the noise of the crowd by walking it past the market.
sceneCN: 这里 accustom 指通过反复经历使对象习惯某种刺激（第 1 个义项：使习惯）；句意为驯犬师每天带幼犬穿过市场，让它习惯人群的声响。

derivatives.zh: 由 accustom 加 -ed 构成，义为「习惯的；惯常的」
由 accustomed 加 un- 构成，义为「不习惯的；不寻常的」

senses.title: To make used to something by repetition
senses.definition: to make a person or animal familiar with a condition by repeating the experience
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复经历，让人或动物对某种状况变得熟悉
senses.example: The trainer accustoms the dog to loud noises before the show.
senses.exampleCN: 驯犬师在演出前让狗习惯巨大的声响。
senses.why: The word is built on custom, a settled practice, so accustoming is turning an experience into a custom.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建在 custom「惯例」之上，所以「使习惯」就是把一段经历变成惯例。

senses.title: To adapt to a new environment
senses.definition: to help a living thing adjust to a climate, place or routine it is not used to
senses.definitionCN: 帮助生物适应它尚不熟悉的气候、地点或常规
senses.example: Gardeners accustom seedlings to open air a few hours at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁每次让幼苗在户外待几个小时，使它适应露天的环境。
senses.why: A new climate is only a new custom of the body, learned by daily exposure.
senses.whyCN: 新的气候不过是身体的一套新惯例，靠每天接触来学会。

senses.title: To make the body tolerate hardship
senses.definition: to train the body to endure cold, height or fatigue without distress
senses.definitionCN: 训练身体耐受寒冷、高度或疲劳而不难受
senses.example: Climbers accustom their bodies to thin air before the final climb.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在最后冲顶前让身体适应稀薄的空气。
senses.why: Repeated exposure teaches the body a habit it cannot be told.
senses.whyCN: 反复接触能教给身体一种无法用言语告知的习惯。

intro.en: Accustom is custom turned into a verb: a practice repeated until it becomes second nature.
intro.cn: accustom 是把 custom「惯例」变成动词：一种做法重复到成为第二天性。

items.en: Consuetudo meant custom or habit, from consuescere, to become used to.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为「惯例、习惯」，出自 consuescere「变得习惯」。

items.en: French costume meant a customary way of doing things, not yet a garment.
items.cn: 法语 costume 当时指「惯常的做法」，还不是「服装」。

items.en: The verb acostumer meant to make someone used to a practice.
items.cn: 动词 acostumer 意为「使某人习惯于某种做法」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb and kept the sense of repeated training.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，保留了「反复训练」的意思。

items.en: The adjective accustomed now also means usual, as in one's accustomed seat.
items.cn: 形容词 accustomed 今天还表示「惯常的」，如「惯常坐的位置」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the custom family; the near-meaning group is the verbs of habituation.
note.cn: 形近组是 custom 词族；近义组是表示习惯化的动词。

entries.definition: A traditional and widely accepted way of behaving.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风俗、惯例」，是本词的词根。

entries.definition: Used to something, or usual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「习惯的；惯常的」。

entries.definition: A person who buys from a shop regularly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾客」，同出 custom 一族但语义已转向买卖。

entries.definition: To make something fit a particular buyer.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「定制」，同根而义转为「按需改造」。

entries.definition: To make someone used to something by long repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使习惯」，最贴近本词的正式同义词。

entries.definition: To make someone know something well.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使熟悉」，侧重了解而非身体适应。

entries.definition: To make someone accept something unpleasant by exposure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使习惯于（艰苦）」，多用于忍耐。

entries.definition: To change in order to fit new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应」，侧重改变自身以合新境。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use custom as the root and accustomed as the everyday adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用 custom 这个词根，以及日常形容词 accustomed。

normal.en: Accustom is custom plus the Latin prefix ad-, to make a custom for someone.
normal.cn: accustom 是 custom 加拉丁前缀 ad-，意为「为某人造一个惯例」。

normal.en: Be accustomed to is the form you will meet most, and it takes to, not with.
normal.cn: 最常遇到的是 be accustomed to，后面接 to，不接 with。

normal.en: The adjective accustomed also means usual: his accustomed chair.
normal.cn: 形容词 accustomed 还表示「惯常的」：他惯常坐的椅子。

normal.en: Unaccustomed means not used to something, and it often precedes to.
normal.cn: unaccustomed 意为「不习惯的」，后面常接 to。

normal.en: The word is about the body and the nerves, not about understanding.
normal.cn: 这个词说的是身体与神经，而不是理解。

abstract.en: A hand that flinches at cold water, then stops flinching by the tenth dip.
abstract.cn: 一只手碰到冷水会缩，泡到第十次就不再缩了。

abstract.en: A path worn into grass by feet that walked it every day.
abstract.cn: 草地上被每天走过的脚踩出的一条小路。

abstract.en: A clock that rings at six until nobody hears it any more.
abstract.cn: 六点响起的钟，响到后来没人再听见。

examples.en: It takes a few weeks to accustom a kitten to a harness.
examples.cn: 让小猫习惯牵引背带需要几周时间。

examples.en: She accustoms herself to cold showers every winter.
examples.cn: 每年冬天她都让自己习惯冷水澡。

examples.en: The troops were accustomed to long marches before the campaign.
examples.cn: 战役开始前，部队已习惯于长途行军。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额卡斯特姆」——额头上贴着「卡斯特姆」标签，贴久了就成了习惯

root: 由古法语 acostumer 借入，源自拉丁语 consuetudo「惯例、习惯」，其动词 consuescere 意为「变得习惯」；词根 custom 至今仍指「风俗、惯例」，故 accustom 即「使某事成为惯例」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses all describe repetition wearing down resistance: a habit, an adaptation to a place, and a body trained to hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在描述重复磨掉抗拒：养成习惯、适应环境，以及把身体训练到能耐受艰苦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the tenth repetition, when the flinch does not come.
core.cn: 核心意象：第十次重复时，那个退缩的动作没有出现。

branches.en: THE HABIT: what is repeated becomes a custom of the person.
branches.cn: 习惯线：被重复的事变成这个人的惯例。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a new climate is learned by daily exposure.
branches.cn: 环境线：新气候靠每天接触来学会。

branches.en: THE BODY: cold and thin air are tolerated only after training.
branches.cn: 身体线：寒冷与稀薄的空气只有训练之后才能耐受。

branches.en: THE LEARNING: habit and adaptation are one process at different scales.
branches.cn: 学习线：习惯与适应是同一过程的不同尺度。

branches.en: THE TRAINING: gardener and climber both repeat until resistance fades.
branches.cn: 训练线：园丁与登山者都重复到抗拒消退。

intro.en: A Latin prefix and a root meaning custom make the verb, and English endings make its family.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀加一个意为「惯例」的词根造出这个动词，英语词尾又造出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuetudo and the French verb acostumer are attested; English records the verb from the fifteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo 与法语动词 acostumer 均有文献可证；英语自十五世纪起记录这个动词。

items.example: It turns a custom toward a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把「惯例」指向某个人。

items.example: It supplies the meaning of the whole verb.
items.exampleCN: 它提供整个动词的意义。

items.example: It is the Latin source of custom.
items.exampleCN: 它是 custom 的拉丁语源头。

items.example: It forms accustomed, the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成日常形容词 accustomed。

items.example: It forms accustoming.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accustoming。

items.example: It forms accustoms.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accustoms。

items.example: It forms unaccustomed, meaning not used to.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unaccustomed，意为「不习惯的」。

items.example: It would form accustomedly, a rare adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它可构成罕见的副词 accustomedly。

derivatives.zh: 由 accustom 加 -ed 构成，义为「习惯的；惯常的」
由 accustomed 加 un- 构成，义为「不习惯的；不寻常的」

definition_zh: 达到；实现；取得；完成
definition_en: to succeed in reaching a goal or producing a result through effort
core_image: 终点线上的一只手，先于身体触到那条线
scene: 马拉松最后一段，那位选手咬住节奏，冲过拱门时手表停在预定的时间。In the last stretch of the marathon the runner held her pace, and when she crossed the arch she had achieved the time she planned.
sceneCN: 这里 achieved 指达到预定的成绩（第 1 个义项：达到目标）；句意为选手在最后一段保持节奏，冲线时正好达成计划中的时间。

derivatives.zh: 由 achieve 加 -ment 构成，义为「成就；达成」
由 achieve 加 -able 构成，义为「可以达成的」
由 achieve 加 -er 构成，义为「有成就的人」

senses.title: To reach a goal
senses.definition: to arrive at a target one has set, after effort or planning
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力或筹划，抵达自己设定的目标
senses.example: The company achieved its sales target two months early.
senses.exampleCN: 公司提前两个月达到了销售目标。
senses.why: The old French verb meant to bring something to a head, so a goal is reached when it is brought to its head.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词意为「把东西带到顶端」，目标被带到顶端，就是被达到了。

senses.title: To produce a result
senses.definition: to obtain a measurable outcome, such as results or growth
senses.definitionCN: 取得可以衡量的结果，如成绩或增长
senses.example: The new method achieved better results with less waste.
senses.exampleCN: 新方法取得了更好的结果，浪费也更少。
senses.why: A result is the head of the effort, the point where work becomes something visible.
senses.whyCN: 结果是努力的那个顶端，是付出变成可见之物的那一点。

senses.title: To overcome difficulty and succeed
senses.definition: to succeed in something that resistance made unlikely
senses.definitionCN: 在阻力使成功变得渺茫时仍然做成
senses.example: The negotiators achieved a settlement after three nights of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过三夜谈判，谈判者促成了一项和解。
senses.why: The word carries a climb, and a climb matters most where the slope is steep.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着一段攀爬，而坡度最陡处，攀爬才最要紧。

senses.title: To gain recognition or status
senses.definition: to win a position, a reputation or respect over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间赢得某种地位、声誉或尊重
senses.example: The composer achieved fame only late in life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作曲家晚年才获得名声。
senses.why: Reputation is a summit reached slowly, and the word keeps that summit in view.
senses.whyCN: 名声是慢慢抵达的高处，这个词始终望着那个高处。

intro.en: Achieve comes from a French phrase about bringing something to a head, and it still means arriving at the top of an effort.
intro.cn: achieve 出自一个法语说法，意为「把东西带到顶端」，至今仍指抵达努力的最高点。

items.en: The phrase ad caput meant to the head, that is, to the top or the end.
items.cn: 短语 ad caput 意为「到头部」，也就是到顶端、到尽头。

items.en: Achever meant to finish, to bring a matter to its head.
items.cn: achever 意为「完成」，把一件事带到它的顶端。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as acheve, meaning to finish or to accomplish.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 acheve，意为「完成、做成」。

items.en: The spelling settled as achieve, and the sense narrowed toward reaching a goal.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 achieve，词义收窄到「达到目标」。

items.en: Today the word covers goals, results, settlements and reputation.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖目标、成果、和解与名声。

note.en: The look-alike group is the achievement family; the near-meaning group is the verbs of attainment.
note.cn: 形近组是 achievement 词族；近义组是表示达成的动词。

entries.definition: Something done successfully, or the act of reaching a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就；达成」。

entries.definition: Possible to reach with reasonable effort.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可以达成的」。

entries.definition: A person who succeeds in reaching goals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有成就的人」。

entries.definition: To complete a task or reach an aim.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成」，侧重任务做完。

entries.definition: To reach a level or obtain something desired.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「达到、获得」，较正式。

entries.definition: To make a plan or hope come true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现」，多指计划成真。

entries.definition: To carry out a promise, duty or dream.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「履行、实现」，多指诺言与梦想。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the French image of bringing something to a head.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用法语里「把东西带到顶端」的画面。

normal.en: The root is a chief, a head: achieve is to bring a matter to its head.
normal.cn: 词根是 chief「头」：achieve 就是把事情带到顶端。

normal.en: Achievement is the noun, achievable the adjective, achiever the person.
normal.cn: 名词是 achievement，形容词是 achievable，人是 achiever。

normal.en: You achieve a goal, a result, a balance or independence; the object is a summit.
normal.cn: achieve 后接目标、成果、平衡或独立；宾语总像一个高处。

normal.en: Do not confuse achieve with receive: one takes effort, the other takes a hand-out.
normal.cn: 不要把 achieve 与 receive 混淆：一个靠努力，一个靠别人给。

normal.en: The past participle achieved often follows have or had in perfect tenses.
normal.cn: 过去分词 achieved 常用于完成时，跟在 have 或 had 之后。

abstract.en: A hand touching the tape a moment before the body arrives.
abstract.cn: 一只手比身体早一瞬触到终点线。

abstract.en: A climber's fingers closing on the last hold of a wall.
abstract.cn: 攀登者的手指扣住墙上最后一个支点。

abstract.en: A sealed letter finally stamped with the word done.
abstract.cn: 一封封好的信终于盖上「完成」的印。

examples.en: She achieved her goal of running the race under four hours.
examples.cn: 她达成了四小时内跑完全程的目标。

examples.en: The team achieved a remarkable result with a small budget.
examples.cn: 团队用很小的预算取得了出色的成果。

examples.en: They achieved peace after years of patient negotiation.
examples.cn: 经过多年耐心谈判，他们实现了和平。

root: 由古法语 achever 借入，源出拉丁语短语 ad caput「到头部」，即「到顶端、到尽头」；词根 chief（头）仍见于 chief 与 achieve 的古义，故 achieve 意为「把事做到顶」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses all describe arriving at the top of an effort: a set goal, a visible result, a difficult settlement, and a slowly won reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都描述抵达努力的最高处：设定的目标、可见的成果、艰难的和解，以及慢慢赢得的声誉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the hand touching the finish line before the body knows it.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体还没反应过来，手已经触到终点线。

branches.en: THE GOAL: a target set in advance and reached.
branches.cn: 目标线：事先设下、后来抵达的靶子。

branches.en: THE RESULT: effort turns into something that can be measured.
branches.cn: 成果线：付出变成可以衡量的东西。

branches.en: THE STRUGGLE: the steeper the slope, the more the word means.
branches.cn: 艰难线：坡越陡，这个词的分量越重。

branches.en: THE SUMMIT: reputation is a height reached late.
branches.cn: 高处线：名声是晚些才抵达的高度。

branches.en: THE HEAD: goal and result are two names for the top of the same climb.
branches.cn: 顶端线：目标与成果，是同一次攀爬顶端的两个名字。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput (head) and French achever are attested; English records the verb from the fourteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput（头）与法语 achever 均有文献可证；英语自十四世纪起记录这个动词。

definition_zh: 成就；成绩；达成；实现
definition_en: something done successfully, especially after effort, or the act of reaching a goal
core_image: 墙上挂着的一枚奖章，背后是没人看见的许多个清晨
scene: 校史馆的玻璃柜里放着一枚旧奖章，解说牌写着获奖者的名字与年份。In the school museum a small medal lies under glass, and the label beside it records the achievement of a former pupil.
sceneCN: 这里 achievement 指那名旧日学生做成的值得纪念之事（第 1 个义项：成就）；句意为玻璃柜里的奖章与标签记录着一位校友的成就。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「达到；实现」

senses.title: Something done successfully
senses.definition: a notable thing a person has done, usually after effort
senses.definitionCN: 一个人经过努力做成的值得称道之事
senses.example: Winning the scholarship was her greatest achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 获得那项奖学金是她最大的成就。
senses.why: The noun names the head of an effort, the point where trying became a result worth naming.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指努力的那个顶端，即付出变成值得一提的结果的那一点。

senses.title: The act of reaching a goal
senses.definition: the process of arriving at a target rather than the target itself
senses.definitionCN: 抵达目标的过程，而不是目标本身
senses.example: The achievement of the target took two full years.
senses.exampleCN: 这一目标的达成用了整整两年。
senses.why: The same noun can look at the climb instead of the summit.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词可以把视线放在攀爬上，而不是山顶上。

senses.title: Measured performance
senses.definition: the level a pupil or worker reaches, as recorded and compared
senses.definitionCN: 学生或员工达到并被记录、比较的水平
senses.example: The school reports on each pupil's achievements every term.
senses.exampleCN: 学校每学期报告每个学生的成绩。
senses.why: Once results are written down, an achievement becomes a figure in a record.
senses.whyCN: 结果一旦被写下，成就就变成记录里的一个数字。

intro.en: Achievement is the noun of achieve, and it turns a climb into something that can be named and displayed.
intro.cn: achievement 是 achieve 的名词，把一次攀爬变成可以命名、可以展示的东西。

items.en: The Latin phrase meant to the head, hence to the top of a matter.
items.cn: 那句拉丁短语意为「到头部」，也就是到一件事的顶端。

items.en: Achever meant to bring a matter to completion.
items.cn: achever 意为「把一件事做到完成」。

items.en: The verb entered English first; the noun followed with the ending -ment.
items.cn: 动词先进英语，名词随后以 -ment 词尾出现。

items.en: Achievement also named a heraldic shield, a coat of arms displayed.
items.cn: 在十六世纪，achievement 还指纹章盾，即展示出来的家徽。

items.en: Today the noun covers personal feats, academic results and lifetime honours.
items.cn: 今天这个名词覆盖个人功业、学业成绩与终身荣誉。

note.en: The look-alike group is the achieve family; the near-meaning group is words for completed feats.
note.cn: 形近组是 achieve 词族；近义组是表示功业的词。

entries.definition: To reach a goal through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「达到、实现」，是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: Possible to accomplish.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可以达成的」。

entries.definition: A person who reaches goals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有成就的人」。

entries.definition: Something completed successfully.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「完成的事、成就」，侧重任务做完。

entries.definition: An impressive act requiring skill or courage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「功绩」，强调技艺或勇气。

entries.definition: The reaching of a level or the thing reached.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「达到、造诣」，较正式。

entries.definition: The achieving of a desired aim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成功」，范围最广。

normalIntro.en: The hooks link the noun to the climb inside the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个名词连到动词里那段攀爬。

normal.en: Achieve plus ment: the thing left after the climbing is done.
normal.cn: achieve 加 ment：攀爬结束后留下的那个东西。

normal.en: A sense of achievement is the feeling at the summit, not the summit itself.
normal.cn: a sense of achievement 是山顶上的感觉，而不是山顶本身。

normal.en: Academic achievement is measured; lifetime achievement is honoured.
normal.cn: 学业成就靠测量，终身成就靠表彰。

normal.en: The word takes of: the achievement of a goal.
normal.cn: 这个词后接 of：the achievement of a goal。

normal.en: Do not use achievement for the effort itself; it names the result or the reaching.
normal.cn: 不要用 achievement 指努力本身；它指结果或抵达。

abstract.en: A medal under glass with a name and a year beside it.
abstract.cn: 玻璃下的一枚奖章，旁边写着名字与年份。

abstract.en: A wall where one framed page hangs among empty hooks.
abstract.cn: 一面墙，一幅装框的纸挂在许多空钩之间。

abstract.en: A hand lifting a cup that is heavier than it looks.
abstract.cn: 一只手举起一只比看上去更重的杯子。

examples.en: The bridge was a remarkable achievement for the small town.
examples.cn: 这座桥对这个小城来说是一项了不起的成就。

examples.en: She took pride in the achievement of her first book.
examples.cn: 她为第一本书的完成感到自豪。

examples.en: The report compares the achievements of pupils across the region.
examples.cn: 这份报告比较了本地区学生的成绩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额奇物门特」——额头上顶着一件奇物，门特一关，才算大功告成

root: 由动词 achieve 加名词后缀 -ment 构成；achieve 出自古法语 achever，源出拉丁语 ad caput「到头部」，故本词指「把事做到顶端所留下的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses look at the same summit from different distances: the feat itself, the climb up to it, and the measured score left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从不同距离看同一座山顶：功业本身、爬上去的过程，以及留下的可测分数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a medal under glass, and all the mornings nobody saw.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃下的一枚奖章，以及没人看见的许多个清晨。

branches.en: THE FEAT: a named thing done successfully.
branches.cn: 功业线：一件做成了、可被命名的事。

branches.en: THE CLIMB: the reaching, seen as a process.
branches.cn: 攀爬线：把抵达看作一个过程。

branches.en: THE RECORD: results written down and compared.
branches.cn: 记录线：结果被写下并加以比较。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: a feat becomes a score once it is recorded.
branches.cn: 证据线：功业一旦被记录，就成了分数。

branches.en: THE HEAD: the top of the effort, whether seen as act or as object.
branches.cn: 顶端线：努力的最高点，无论看成动作还是看成物件。

definition_en: a chemical substance that reacts with metals and bases, or something sour and sharp
core_image: 舌尖碰到柠檬的一瞬，整张脸都缩了起来
scene: 实验室里那只瓶子贴着一道警示标签，老师要求学生戴上手套再打开。In the laboratory the bottle carried a warning label, and the teacher told the class to wear gloves before handling the acid.
sceneCN: 这里 acid 指具有腐蚀性的酸性化学物质（第 1 个义项：化学上的酸）；句意为实验室里那只瓶子贴有警示，老师要求学生戴手套再碰这种酸。

senses.title: A chemical that reacts with bases
senses.definition: a substance that gives up hydrogen ions and reacts with metals and bases
senses.definitionCN: 能释放氢离子、与金属和碱发生反应的物质
senses.example: The acid in the battery must never touch the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 电池里的酸绝不能碰到皮肤。
senses.why: The Latin word for sour named the taste first, and chemistry later borrowed it for substances that taste that way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里表示「酸」的词先命名味道，化学后来借它指具有那种味道的物质。

senses.title: A sour substance in food
senses.definition: a natural acid found in fruit, vinegar or fermented food
senses.definitionCN: 水果、醋或发酵食物中天然存在的酸
senses.example: Lemon juice owes its sharpness to citric acid.
senses.exampleCN: 柠檬汁的锐利酸味来自柠檬酸。
senses.why: The kitchen keeps the oldest sense of the word alive.
senses.whyCN: 厨房让这个词最古老的意义一直活着。

senses.title: Sour in taste
senses.definition: having a sharp taste like lemon or vinegar
senses.definitionCN: 具有柠檬或醋那样尖锐的味道
senses.example: The unripe apple had a distinctly acid taste.
senses.exampleCN: 那只未熟的苹果有明显的酸味。
senses.why: The adjective is the taste itself, before any chemistry was known.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是味道本身，那时还没有化学。

senses.title: Bitter and cutting in tone
senses.definition: of words or humour, sharp in a way that wounds
senses.definitionCN: 指言语或幽默尖锐得会伤人
senses.example: Her acid remark ended the conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 她那句尖刻的话终结了谈话。
senses.why: Sourness on the tongue became sourness in the voice, and both make the face contract.
senses.whyCN: 舌尖上的酸变成声音里的酸，两者都让人皱起脸。

intro.en: Acid is a taste word that chemistry adopted: sour on the tongue first, sharp in the voice later.
intro.cn: acid 是一个被化学借走的味道词：先在舌尖上酸，后在言语中尖。

items.en: The verb acere meant to be sour or sharp.
items.cn: 动词 acere 意为「是酸的、是尖的」。

items.en: The adjective acidus meant sour, and also sharp to the senses.
items.cn: 形容词 acidus 意为「酸的」，也指感官上的尖锐。

items.en: The related adjective acer meant keen, sharp, piercing.
items.cn: 相关形容词 acer 意为「锐利的、刺人的」。

items.en: French took the Latin adjective as acide and passed it to English.
items.cn: 法语把那个拉丁形容词作 acide，再传给英语。

items.en: English used it for sour things long before it named a chemical class.
items.cn: 英语很久以前就用它形容酸的东西，远早于它命名化学类别。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acid family; the near-meaning group is words for sourness and sharpness.
note.cn: 形近组是 acid 词族；近义组是表示酸与尖锐的词。

entries.definition: Having the properties of an acid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸性的」。

entries.definition: The quality of being acid, or the amount of acid present.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸性；酸度」。

entries.definition: To make something acid or more acid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使酸化」。

entries.definition: A condition in which the blood is too acid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸中毒」，指血液酸性过强。

entries.definition: Having a sharp taste like lemon.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸的」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: Pleasantly sharp in taste.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸得爽口的」，多含褒义。

entries.definition: Able to burn, or bitterly sarcastic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腐蚀性的」，也指「刻薄的」。

entries.definition: Sharp and painful, of cold or words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「刺人的」，可用于寒风或言语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the sour taste, the chemistry, and the sharp tongue.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用酸味、化学，以及那张尖刻的嘴。

normal.en: The root ac- means sharp, and acid is sharpness you can taste.
normal.cn: 词根 ac- 意为「尖」，acid 就是尝得到的尖锐。

normal.en: Acid rain is named by its chemistry, not by its taste.
normal.cn: 酸雨是按化学成分命名的，不是按味道。

normal.en: Acidity is the noun, acidic the adjective, acidify the verb.
normal.cn: 名词是 acidity，形容词是 acidic，动词是 acidify。

normal.en: An acid test is originally a chemical check, now any severe trial.
normal.cn: acid test 原指化学检验，现在泛指严峻考验。

normal.en: An acid remark is sourness moved from the tongue to the temper.
normal.cn: acid remark 是酸味从舌头搬到了脾气上。

abstract.en: A lemon wedge pressed until the face folds.
abstract.cn: 一瓣柠檬被挤到脸都皱起来。

abstract.en: A drop of liquid eating a dark hole in metal.
abstract.cn: 一滴液体在金属上啃出一个黑洞。

abstract.en: A voice so dry that the room goes quiet.
abstract.cn: 一个干涩得让房间安静下来的声音。

examples.en: The acid in the soil prevents most crops from growing.
examples.cn: 土壤里的酸使大多数作物无法生长。

examples.en: Vinegar is a mild acid used in cooking.
examples.cn: 醋是一种用于烹饪的弱酸。

examples.en: He made an acid comment about the plan and left.
examples.cn: 他对这个计划说了句尖刻的话就走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱吸的」——爱吸的那种东西，吸一口酸得皱眉

root: 源自拉丁语 acidus「酸的」，出自动词 acere「是酸的」，并与 acer「锐利的」同源；词根 ac- 表「尖、锐」，故酸味与尖刻同出一源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses move from chemistry to the kitchen to the tongue to the temper: a reacting substance, a sour food acid, a sour taste, and a cutting remark.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从化学走到厨房、舌头与脾气：参与反应的物质、食物里的酸、酸味，以及尖刻的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the face contracting at the first touch of lemon.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚碰到柠檬时整张脸缩起来。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY: a substance that reacts and gives up ions.
branches.cn: 化学线：参与反应并释放离子的物质。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN: fruit and vinegar keep the oldest sense alive.
branches.cn: 厨房线：水果与醋让最古老的意义活着。

branches.en: THE TONGUE: the taste itself, sharp and contracting.
branches.cn: 舌尖线：味道本身，尖锐得让人缩脸。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: the same sharpness moved into speech.
branches.cn: 脾气线：同一种尖锐搬进了言语。

branches.en: THE SHARP: chemistry and taste are two readings of one quality.
branches.cn: 尖锐线：化学与味觉，是对同一种性质的两套读法。

intro.en: One Latin root meaning sharp runs through the taste, the chemistry and the tone.
intro.cn: 一个意为「尖」的拉丁词根，贯穿味道、化学与语气。

latinIntro.en: Latin acere, acidus and acer are attested; English records the word from the thirteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acere、acidus 与 acer 均有文献可证；英语自十三世纪起记录这个词。

definition_zh: 承认；确认收到；致谢；认可；理会
definition_en: to accept that something is true, to confirm that something has arrived, or to show that someone has been noticed
core_image: 收到信后回一张卡片，让对方知道自己确实看到了
scene: 编辑部收到投稿，第二天寄回一张明信片，上面写着稿件已到。The editorial office receives a submission and sends back a card the next day to acknowledge that the manuscript has arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 acknowledge 指正式确认收到（第 2 个义项：确认收到）；句意为编辑部收到投稿后第二天寄回明信片，确认稿件已经送到。

derivatives.zh: 由 acknowledge 加 -ment 构成，义为「承认；致谢；收据」
由 acknowledge 加 -ed 构成，义为「公认的」

senses.title: To admit that something is true
senses.definition: to accept, often unwillingly, that a fact or fault is real
senses.definitionCN: 接受某个事实或过错确实存在，常带不情愿
senses.example: I acknowledge that the delay was my fault.
senses.exampleCN: 我承认这次延误是我的错。
senses.why: The word grows from knowledge: to acknowledge is to say yes to what one already knows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「知道」长出来：承认就是把已经知道的事说一声「是」。

senses.title: To confirm that something has arrived
senses.definition: to tell a sender formally that a letter, order or message has been received
senses.definitionCN: 正式告知发件人，信件、订单或消息已经送达
senses.example: Please acknowledge receipt of this letter within three days.
senses.exampleCN: 请在三天内确认收到此信。
senses.why: A reply card turns private knowledge into a record the other side can see.
senses.whyCN: 一张回执把私下的知道变成对方看得见的记录。

senses.title: To express thanks for help
senses.definition: to name someone publicly as a source of help or support
senses.definitionCN: 公开点出某人的帮助或支持并表示感谢
senses.example: The author acknowledges the help of the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 作者感谢研究团队的帮助。
senses.why: Knowing who helped and saying so is the same act of recognition.
senses.whyCN: 知道谁帮了忙，并把这份知道说出来，是同一种「认出」。

senses.title: To recognize someone's status
senses.definition: to treat a person, office or claim as valid and worthy
senses.definitionCN: 把某人、某个职位或某种主张视为有效、值得尊重
senses.example: The government refused to acknowledge the new state.
senses.exampleCN: 该国政府拒绝承认这个新国家。
senses.why: Recognition here is legal, but it still rests on the same acknowledgement of what is there.
senses.whyCN: 这里的认可是法律上的，但仍建立在同一个「承认它就在那里」的动作上。

senses.title: To notice and respond to someone
senses.definition: to show by a word or a look that one has seen a person
senses.definitionCN: 用一句话或一个眼神表示自己看见了某人
senses.example: She walked past me without acknowledging my greeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她从我身边走过，没有理会我的问候。
senses.why: Even a nod is a receipt: I have received you.
senses.whyCN: 即使只是一个点头，也是一张回执：我收到了你。

intro.en: Acknowledge is an English word built on knowledge, with a prefix that means toward.
intro.cn: acknowledge 是一个建在 knowledge 上的英语词，前缀表示「朝向」。

items.en: Oncnāwan meant to recognize or understand a thing.
items.cn: oncnāwan 意为「认出、明白」一件事。

items.en: Knowledge named the state of knowing, and the verb grew beside the noun.
items.cn: knowledge 指「知道」的状态，动词就在这个名词旁边长出来。

items.en: The form acknowledge appeared with the prefix ac- and the ending -ledge.
items.cn: acknowledge 这一形式出现，带前缀 ac- 与词尾 -ledge。

items.en: The legal sense of acknowledging a deed or a debt developed in this period.
items.cn: 承认契约或债务的法律义在这一时期发展起来。

items.en: Today the word covers admissions, receipts, thanks and simple recognition.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖承认、回执、致谢与简单的理会。

note.en: The look-alike group is the knowledge family; the near-meaning group is the verbs of admitting.
note.cn: 形近组是 knowledge 词族；近义组是表示承认的动词。

entries.definition: The facts and understanding a person has.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「知识」，是本词的构词基座。

entries.definition: An act of admitting or thanking, or a receipt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认；致谢；回执」。

entries.definition: Having a great deal of information.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「博学的」，同出 knowledge 一族。

entries.definition: To accept that something is true, often unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认」，常带不情愿。

entries.definition: To admit a point after resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「让步承认」，先有争辩。

entries.definition: To accept something as valid or familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「认出、认可」，侧重确认其有效性。

entries.definition: To admit a fault or a secret.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坦白」，多指过错或秘密。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on knowledge plus a prefix of direction, and on the receipt image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建在 knowledge 加方向前缀上，也建在回执的画面上。

normal.en: Knowledge plus ac-: to acknowledge is to send knowledge back toward someone.
normal.cn: knowledge 加 ac-：承认就是把「知道」朝某人送回去。

normal.en: Acknowledge receipt is the phrase on every formal reply.
normal.cn: acknowledge receipt 是每封正式回函上的固定说法。

normal.en: The noun is acknowledgement, and it can mean a thank-you page in a book.
normal.cn: 名词是 acknowledgement，也可以指书前的致谢页。

normal.en: Acknowledge defeat is to admit the result without waiting to be asked.
normal.cn: acknowledge defeat 是不等别人问就认下结果。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with know: one is the state, the other is the public act.
normal.cn: 不要与 know 混淆：一个是状态，一个是公开的动作。

abstract.en: A postcard mailed back the day a parcel arrives.
abstract.cn: 包裹到的当天就寄回一张明信片。

abstract.en: A nod across a crowded room, enough to say I see you.
abstract.cn: 挤满人的房间里一个点头，足以说「我看见你了」。

abstract.en: A name printed at the top of a page of thanks.
abstract.cn: 一页致谢文字开头印着的名字。

examples.en: Please acknowledge receipt of this order by email.
examples.cn: 请用电子邮件确认收到此订单。

examples.en: He refused to acknowledge that the plan had failed.
examples.cn: 他拒绝承认这个计划已经失败。

examples.en: The paper acknowledges the support of several foundations.
examples.cn: 论文致谢了几家基金会的支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额克诺里奇」——额头上贴着「诺里奇」的回执，表示已经收到

root: 由 know 与 knowledge 一族构成，前缀 ac- 表「朝向」，词尾 -ledge 与 knowledge 同源；古英语 oncnāwan 意为「认出」，故本词是「把知道的事公开认下或回给对方」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all perform one act, saying yes to what one knows: a fact, a delivery, a helper, a state, or a person in the room.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都在做同一个动作——对自己知道的事说「是」：事实、送达、援手、一个国家，或房间里的某个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reply card that proves the message landed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张回执，证明消息确实落到了。

branches.en: THE FACT: what one knows is said out loud.
branches.cn: 事实线：已经知道的事被说出声。

branches.en: THE RECEIPT: the reply proves delivery.
branches.cn: 回执线：回音证明东西送到了。

branches.en: THE THANKS: a helper is named in public.
branches.cn: 致谢线：帮忙的人被公开点名。

branches.en: THE STATUS: a state or office is accepted as real.
branches.cn: 地位线：一个国家或职位被当作真的。

branches.en: THE NOD: even a glance can carry the receipt.
branches.cn: 点头线：一个眼神也能递出回执。

intro.en: An English noun of knowing plus a Latin-shaped prefix made this verb.
intro.cn: 一个表示「知道」的英语名词，加上一个拉丁式前缀，造出了这个动词。

latinIntro.en: Old English oncnāwan is attested; the modern form is English, not Latin, though it looks Latinate.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 oncnāwan 有文献可证；现代形式是英语自身的产物，虽然看着像拉丁词。

items.exampleCN: 它把「承认」朝某人送回去。

items.example: It supplies the core meaning.
items.exampleCN: 它提供核心意义。

items.example: It is the oldest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个家族最老的成员。

items.example: It is the Old English ancestor of the idea.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一概念的古英语祖先。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 knowledge 与 acknowledge 里。

items.example: It forms acknowledgement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acknowledgement。

items.example: It forms acknowledged, also an adjective meaning recognized.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acknowledged，也作形容词表示「公认的」。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 acknowledging。
