definition_zh: 使熟悉；使了解；告知
definition_en: to make someone familiar with a person, place or fact
core_image: 把一个人领进一间陌生的屋子，逐一介绍每样东西
scene: 新来的实习生第一周由老员工带着，逐个部门走一遍。In her first week the new intern was shown round by an old employee, who took her from office to office to acquaint her with the building.
sceneCN: 这里 acquaint 指带她熟悉这栋楼（第 1 个义项：使熟悉）；句意为老员工在头一周带实习生逐个部门走动，让她认识各处。

collocations.phrase: acquaint a person with the facts

derivatives.zh: 由 acquaint 加 -ance 构成，义为「熟人；了解」
由 acquaint 加 -ed 构成，义为「熟悉的；相识的」

senses.title: To make someone familiar with something
senses.definition: to give a person knowledge of a place, system or subject by guiding them through it
senses.definitionCN: 带着某人走一遍，使其对某地、某制度或某学科有所认识
senses.example: The guide will acquaint you with the old quarter of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 导游会带你熟悉老城区。
senses.why: The Latin source meant to make known, so the verb is a bringing-into-knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「使被知道」，所以这个动词就是把某人带进「知道」里。

senses.title: To inform someone of a fact
senses.definition: to tell a person the details they need to know
senses.definitionCN: 把对方需要知道的情况告诉他
senses.example: The officer acquainted us with the new regulations.
senses.exampleCN: 那位官员向我们说明了新规定。
senses.why: A fact can be handed over as directly as a room can be shown.
senses.whyCN: 事实可以像房间一样，直接领着对方看一遍。

senses.title: To be familiar through contact
senses.definition: in the passive, to have met someone or to know something slightly
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动结构，指与某人见过面，或对某事略有所知
senses.example: I am acquainted with one of the witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 我认识其中一位证人。
senses.why: Once the introduction is done, the state of being acquainted is what remains.
senses.whyCN: 介绍一旦完成，留下来的状态就是「已相识」。

intro.en: Acquaint is a French verb built on the Latin word for known.
intro.cn: acquaint 是一个建在拉丁语「已知」一词上的法语动词。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to come to know, and its participle cognitus meant known.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为「逐渐知道」，其分词 cognitus 意为「已知的」。

items.en: A later Latin form meant to make someone know something.
items.cn: 较晚的拉丁形式意为「使某人知道某事」。

items.en: French acointier meant to make known or to bring into contact.
items.cn: 法语 acointier 意为「使知道」或「使接触」。

items.en: English borrowed it as aquaint, later acquaint.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 aquaint，后来定型为 acquaint。

items.en: The verb now survives mainly in the phrase be acquainted with.
items.cn: 这个动词今天主要活在 be acquainted with 这一短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acquaintance family; the near-meaning group is the verbs of informing.
note.cn: 形近组是 acquaintance 词族；近义组是表示告知的动词。

entries.definition: A person one knows slightly, or knowledge of a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「熟人」或「对某事的了解」。

entries.definition: Familiar with someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟悉的；相识的」。

entries.definition: Attractively old-fashioned; from the same Latin word for known.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「古雅别致的」，与本源共享拉丁语「已知」一词。

entries.definition: To make someone know something well.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使熟悉」，最贴近的同义词。

entries.definition: To give someone facts they need.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告知」，侧重传递事实。

entries.definition: To bring a person into contact with another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「介绍」，使人彼此接触。

entries.definition: To give someone the essential facts before a task.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「简要通报」，多用于任务之前。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin known and the passive phrase that keeps the verb alive.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用拉丁语「已知」，以及让这个动词活着的被动短语。

normal.en: The root is the Latin word for known, so to acquaint is to make known.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语「已知」，所以 acquaint 就是「使人知道」。

normal.en: Be acquainted with is the phrase you will actually use; it takes with.
normal.cn: 实际最常用的是 be acquainted with，介词用 with。

normal.en: The noun acquaintance means both a person and a degree of knowledge.
normal.cn: 名词 acquaintance 既指一个人，也指了解的程度。

normal.en: Acquaint yourself with the rules is formal advice to read them.
normal.cn: acquaint yourself with the rules 是让人去读规则的正式说法。

normal.en: Do not say acquaint to a person; the thing known takes with.
normal.cn: 不要说 acquaint to somebody，所知之物要用 with 引出。

abstract.en: A guide walking a newcomer from room to room.
abstract.cn: 一位向导领着新来的人一间间走。

abstract.en: A hand laid on a strange door handle for the first time.
abstract.cn: 一只手第一次按上陌生的门把。

abstract.en: A map folded open on a table while a finger traces the route.
abstract.cn: 地图在桌上摊开，一根手指沿着路线走。

examples.en: You should acquaint yourself with the safety rules first.
examples.cn: 你应当先熟悉安全规则。

examples.en: The booklet acquaints visitors with the history of the house.
examples.cn: 这本小册子让来访者了解这座宅子的历史。

examples.en: I became acquainted with her through a mutual friend.
examples.cn: 我通过一位共同的朋友认识了她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额快特」——额头上贴着「快特」通行证，一进门就有人带你熟悉各处

root: 由古法语 acointier 借入，源自拉丁语 cognoscere「逐渐知道」的分词 cognitus「已知的」，前缀 ad- 表「朝向」；故本词意为「使某人进入已知的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses move from guiding a person through a place, to handing over facts, to the state of being familiar afterwards.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从带人走一遍地方，走到把事实交给他，再到事后那种「已熟悉」的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stranger walked from room to room until nothing is unknown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个陌生人被一间间带着走，直到没有一处不认识。

branches.en: THE TOUR: a place is made known by walking it.
branches.cn: 走一遍线：地方靠脚步熟悉。

branches.en: THE FACTS: what is needed is handed over in words.
branches.cn: 事实线：需要知道的东西用话说给对方。

branches.en: THE STATE: after the introduction, familiarity remains.
branches.cn: 状态线：介绍之后，留下的是熟悉。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: an outsider becomes someone who knows.
branches.cn: 转变线：门外人变成知道的人。

branches.en: THE KNOWING: facts and familiarity are the same gift at two depths.
branches.cn: 知线：事实与熟悉，是同一份礼物在两种深浅上。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction plus a root meaning known built the French verb that English borrowed.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀加一个意为「已知」的词根，造出了英语借入的那个法语动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cognoscere and French acointier are attested; English records the verb from the thirteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cognoscere 与法语 acointier 均有文献可证；英语自十三世纪起记录这个动词。

items.exampleCN: 它把「知道」指向某个人。

items.example: It supplies the core of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 它提供意义的核心。

items.example: It is the verb behind the participle.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个分词背后的动词。

definition_en: a person one knows slightly, or a limited knowledge of a subject
core_image: 走廊里点头打招呼的两个人，彼此知道名字却说不清对方的近况
scene: 年会上有人拍他的肩膀，两人聊了几句天气，转身各自去找更熟的朋友。At the annual dinner a man tapped his shoulder, they spoke about the weather for a minute, and each turned away to find closer friends, as acquaintances do.
sceneCN: 这里 acquaintances 指只算点头之交的人（第 1 个义项：熟人）；句意为两人只聊了几句天气，便各自去找更亲近的朋友。

senses.title: A person one knows slightly
senses.definition: someone whose name and face one knows, but not closely
senses.definitionCN: 知道名字和长相、但并不亲近的人
senses.example: She is a business acquaintance rather than a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 她算是生意上的熟人，而不是朋友。
senses.why: The noun names the state left after an introduction: known, but only partly.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指介绍之后留下的状态：知道，但只知道一部分。

senses.title: Limited knowledge of a subject
senses.definition: a degree of familiarity with a field, usually modest
senses.definitionCN: 对某一领域有一定熟悉，通常程度不深
senses.example: I have some acquaintance with the local dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 我对当地方言略有所知。
senses.why: Knowing a person slightly and knowing a subject slightly are the same half-light.
senses.whyCN: 略识一人与略知一门，是同一种半明半暗。

senses.title: The relationship of having met
senses.definition: the state of two people being known to each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个人彼此认识的状态
senses.example: Their acquaintance began at a conference in Beijing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的相识始于北京的一次会议。
senses.why: The word can name the connection itself, not only the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指那层关系本身，而不只是关系中的人。

intro.en: Acquaintance is the noun of acquaint, and it keeps the half-known state of an introduction.
intro.cn: acquaintance 是 acquaint 的名词，保留着介绍之后那种「知道一半」的状态。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to come to know.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为「逐渐知道」。

items.en: The French verb meant to bring someone into knowledge of another.
items.cn: 那个法语动词意为「使某人知道另一人」。

items.en: The French noun named the state of being known to someone.
items.cn: 法语名词指「为某人所知」的状态。

items.en: English borrowed the noun and used it for both people and knowledge.
items.cn: 英语借入这个名词，既指人，也指了解。

items.en: Today it usually means a slight acquaintance, rarely a close one.
items.cn: 今天它通常指浅浅的相识，很少指亲近关系。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acquaint family; the near-meaning group is words for social contact.
note.cn: 形近组是 acquaint 词族；近义组是表示社交接触的词。

entries.definition: To make someone familiar with something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使熟悉」，是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: Familiar with a person or subject.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟悉的；相识的」。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned in an attractive way.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「古雅别致的」，同出拉丁语「已知」一词。

entries.definition: A person one can reach for help or information.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联系人」，强调可以联系到的人。

entries.definition: A person connected with one through work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同事、伙伴」，关系较正式。

entries.definition: The state of knowing something well.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「熟悉」，程度比本词深。

entries.definition: A person one knows who can be useful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「人脉、关系」，带实用色彩。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the half-known state and the -ance noun ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子扣住「知道一半」的状态，以及 -ance 这一名词词尾。

normal.en: Acquaint plus ance: the state of being partly known.
normal.cn: acquaint 加 ance：处于被知道一部分的状态。

normal.en: An acquaintance is not a friend; the word measures distance.
normal.cn: acquaintance 不是朋友，这个词量的是距离。

normal.en: Make an acquaintance is the verb phrase; the noun takes make.
normal.cn: 结识某人说 make an acquaintance，动词用 make。

normal.en: Acquaintance with a subject means a little knowledge, not mastery.
normal.cn: acquaintance with 一门学问指略知，而非精通。

normal.en: On first acquaintance means judging someone before knowing them well.
normal.cn: on first acquaintance 意为在还不熟时就作判断。

abstract.en: Two people nodding in a corridor, each forgetting the other's job.
abstract.cn: 两个人在走廊点头，各自记不清对方做什么工作。

abstract.en: A name in a phone book with no notes beside it.
abstract.cn: 电话簿里的一个名字，旁边没有任何备注。

abstract.en: A doorway one has passed but never entered.
abstract.cn: 一扇走过却从没进去的门。

examples.en: He is an old acquaintance from my university days.
examples.cn: 他是我大学时代的一位旧识。

examples.en: I have only a slight acquaintance with the subject.
examples.cn: 我对这个学科只略知一二。

examples.en: They renewed their acquaintance at the trade fair.
examples.cn: 他们在交易会上重续旧识。

root: 由古法语 acointaunce 借入，是 acointier「使知道」的名词形式，源出拉丁语 cognoscere「逐渐知道」；故本词指「知道一半」的状态与人。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses describe one half-light: a person known by name, a subject known a little, and the relationship that holds two such people.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项描述同一种半明半暗：知道名字的人、略知一二的学问，以及把两人连住的那层关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nod in a corridor, with no story behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：走廊里的一个点头，背后没有故事。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a face and a name, nothing more.
branches.cn: 人物线：一张脸和一个名字，仅此而已。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: a field entered but not mastered.
branches.cn: 学问线：进过门，却未精通。

branches.en: THE RELATION: the thread between two partly known people.
branches.cn: 关系线：两个半熟之人之间的那根线。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE: acquaintances form the outer ring of a social world.
branches.cn: 圈子线：熟人围成社交世界的外圈。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a person and a subject can both be known to a degree.
branches.cn: 程度线：人和学问都能被「知道到某个程度」。

intro.en: A French noun ending turned the verb of knowing into the state of being slightly known.
intro.cn: 一个法语名词词尾，把「使人知道」的动词变成「被略知」的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin cognoscere and French acointaunce are attested; English records the noun from the fourteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cognoscere 与法语 acointaunce 均有文献可证；英语自十四世纪起记录这个名词。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成表状态的名词。

items.example: It is the deepest layer of meaning.
items.exampleCN: 它是最深的一层意义。

items.example: It is the source of the French verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个法语动词的源头。

items.example: It forms acquaintances.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquainted。

items.example: It shares the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它与本源共享同一个拉丁词根。

items.example: It is the everyday cousin of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个家族最日常的亲戚。

definition_zh: 获得；取得；学到；收购；染上
definition_en: to obtain something, often by effort, purchase or gradual experience
core_image: 空着的书架一格一格被填满，每本书都经过挑选
scene: 那家小公司用了三年时间，把街对面的竞争对手连同其仓库一起买了下来。In three years the small company acquired its rival across the street, together with the rival's warehouse.
sceneCN: 这里 acquired 指通过买下对方而取得资产（第 3 个义项：收购）；句意为这家小公司三年内收购了对街的竞争对手及其仓库。

derivatives.zh: 由 acquire 加 -ition 构成，义为「获得；收购；习得」
由 acquire 加 -itive 构成，义为「贪得的；爱收购的」
由 acquire 加 -ed 构成，义为「后天获得的」

senses.title: To obtain something by effort
senses.definition: to come to have something through work, payment or search
senses.definitionCN: 通过劳动、支付或寻找而拥有某物
senses.example: She acquired a small collection of early maps.
senses.exampleCN: 她收集到了一小批古地图。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to seek in addition, so acquiring is the end of a search.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「另外去寻取」，所以获得是一段寻找的终点。

senses.title: To learn a skill or knowledge
senses.definition: to come to possess a skill or body of knowledge gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐掌握一门技能或一门知识
senses.example: Children acquire language without formal lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童不用正式上课就能习得语言。
senses.why: What is learned settles into a person the way a bought object settles into a house.
senses.whyCN: 学到的东西落进一个人心里，就像买来的东西落进一所房子。

senses.title: To buy a company or asset
senses.definition: of a firm, to take over another company or a large asset
senses.definitionCN: 指企业买下另一家公司或一项大型资产
senses.example: The group acquired three regional banks in one year.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团一年内收购了三家地区银行。
senses.why: In business the search ends with a signature and a transfer of ownership.
senses.whyCN: 在商场上，寻找以一次签字和一次产权转移收尾。

senses.title: To develop a habit
senses.definition: to let a habit or taste grow in oneself over time
senses.definitionCN: 让某种习惯或爱好随时间在自己身上长成
senses.example: He acquired the habit of walking before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 他养成了早饭前散步的习惯。
senses.why: A habit is acquired rather than chosen, which is why the verb fits it so well.
senses.whyCN: 习惯是被「取得」的，而不是被挑选的，所以这个动词格外贴切。

senses.title: To contract a disease or condition
senses.definition: to come to suffer from an illness or a physical condition
senses.definitionCN: 开始患上某种疾病或身体状况
senses.example: The patient acquired the infection in hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 病人在医院里染上了这种感染。
senses.why: Something unwanted can also be acquired, as quietly as a habit.
senses.whyCN: 不想要的东西也会被「取得」，其悄无声息一如习惯。

intro.en: Acquire comes from a Latin verb meaning to seek in addition, and every sense ends a kind of search.
intro.cn: acquire 出自一个意为「另外去寻取」的拉丁动词，每个义项都结束一段寻找。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, to ask, to try to obtain.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻找、询问、设法得到」。

items.en: The compound acquirere added ad-, toward, and meant to get in addition.
items.cn: 复合词 acquirere 加上 ad-「朝向」，意为「额外取得」。

items.en: French kept the verb with the same sense of obtaining.
items.cn: 法语保留了这个动词，意义仍是「取得」。

items.en: English borrowed it, at first mainly for property and knowledge.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，最初主要用于财产与知识。

items.en: Commerce added the takeover sense, and medicine added the sense of catching an illness.
items.cn: 商业添上「收购」义，医学添上「染上疾病」义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acquisition family; the near-meaning group is the verbs of getting.
note.cn: 形近组是 acquisition 词族；近义组是表示取得的动词。

entries.definition: The act of obtaining, or the thing obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获得；收购物」。

entries.definition: Eager to own and collect things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「贪得的、爱收集的」。

entries.definition: To need something; from the same Latin verb for seeking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「需要」，与本源共享拉丁语「寻找」一词。

entries.definition: To get something, often by effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，较正式。

entries.definition: To get something useful or valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，多指有益之物。

entries.definition: To buy something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「购买」，比 buy 正式。

entries.definition: To succeed in getting something after effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「争取到」，强调经过努力。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the Latin seek and the objects people usually acquire.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子顺着拉丁语「寻找」，以及人们常取得的那些东西。

normal.en: The root quaerere means to seek, so acquire is a search that ends in possession.
normal.cn: 词根 quaerere 意为「寻找」，所以 acquire 是以占有收尾的寻找。

normal.en: Knowledge, skills, habits and tastes are all acquired; the verb likes the gradual.
normal.cn: 知识、技能、习惯与口味都是 acquired 的；这个动词偏爱「渐渐」。

normal.en: In business, acquire means buy and take over, as in mergers and acquisitions.
normal.cn: 在商业里，acquire 意为买下并接管，如并购一语中的用法。

normal.en: The adjective acquired means gained after birth, as opposed to inherited.
normal.cn: 形容词 acquired 意为「后天获得的」，与「遗传的」相对。

normal.en: Do not say acquire to somebody; the thing is acquired, not the person.
normal.cn: 不要说 acquire somebody；被取得的是物，不是人。

abstract.en: A shelf filling one book at a time, each chosen on purpose.
abstract.cn: 一格一格填满的书架，每本都是特意挑的。

abstract.en: A hand closing around a key that was hard to find.
abstract.cn: 一只手握紧一把找了很久的钥匙。

abstract.en: A habit settling into a body the way dust settles on a ledge.
abstract.cn: 习惯落进身体，像灰尘落在窗台上。

examples.en: She acquired most of her knowledge from old newspapers.
examples.cn: 她的知识大部分来自旧报纸。

examples.en: The firm acquired a smaller rival last spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年春天收购了一个较小的对手。

examples.en: He acquired the habit of checking the locks twice.
examples.cn: 他养成了把门锁检查两遍的习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额快尔」——额头上贴着一张「快尔」的寻物单，找到了就归自己

root: 源自拉丁语 acquirere「额外取得」，由 ad-（朝向）加 quaerere（寻找、询问）构成；古法语作 aquerre，英语十五世纪借入；词根 quaerere 亦见于 require 与 inquiry。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses end five kinds of search: an object, a skill, a company, a habit, and an illness that finds its way in.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项结束五种寻找：一件东西、一门技能、一家公司、一个习惯，以及悄悄找上门的疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf that fills up one chosen object at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一格一格被填满的书架，每件都是挑过的。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a search ends in ownership.
branches.cn: 实物线：寻找以拥有收尾。

branches.en: THE MIND: skills settle in without a receipt.
branches.cn: 心智线：技能进了心里，却没有收据。

branches.en: THE COMPANY: ownership changes hands by signature.
branches.cn: 公司线：所有权靠签字易手。

branches.en: THE HABIT: what is repeated becomes part of a person.
branches.cn: 习惯线：被重复的事成为人的一部分。

branches.en: THE ILLNESS: something unwanted can be acquired too.
branches.cn: 疾病线：不想要的东西也会被「取得」。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction and a Latin verb of seeking built the word, and English endings built its family.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀加一个寻找动词造出这个词，英语词尾又造出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere and acquirere are attested; English records the verb from the fifteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere 与 acquirere 均有文献可证；英语自十五世纪起记录这个动词。

items.example: It adds the idea of getting toward oneself.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「往自己这边取得」的意思。

items.example: It supplies the search inside the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词内部的「寻找」。

items.example: It forms acquisition.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquisition。

items.example: It forms acquisitive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquisitive。

items.example: It forms acquired, also an adjective meaning gained after birth.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquired，也作形容词表示「后天获得的」。

items.example: It forms acquiring.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquiring。

items.example: It forms acquires.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquires。

items.example: It uses the same Latin verb of seeking.
items.exampleCN: 它用的是同一个表示「寻找」的拉丁动词。

definition_zh: 获得；收购；获得物；习得
definition_en: the act of obtaining something, the thing obtained, or a company bought by another
core_image: 签字桌上两份文件叠在一起，一把钥匙从一只手交到另一只手
scene: 博物馆在年底公布，一批私人收藏已由基金会买下并运抵库房。At the end of the year the museum announced that a private collection had been bought by its foundation and moved into the store, its most important acquisition in a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 acquisition 指新购进的藏品（第 3 个义项：获得物）；句意为博物馆年底宣布，一批私人收藏已被买下并运入库房，是十年来最重要的一批藏品。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「获得；收购」
由 acquire 加 -itive 构成，义为「贪得的」

senses.title: The act of obtaining
senses.definition: the process of coming to have something, especially by effort
senses.definitionCN: 取得某物的过程，尤指经过努力
senses.example: The acquisition of the land took years of negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 取得这块地用了多年谈判。
senses.why: The noun takes the verb's search and turns it into a process that can be described.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把动词里的寻找变成一个可以描述的过程。

senses.title: A company bought by another
senses.definition: the purchase of one business by another
senses.definitionCN: 一家企业买下另一家企业
senses.example: The takeover was the largest acquisition in the industry that year.
senses.exampleCN: 这次接管是当年该行业最大的一笔收购。
senses.why: Ownership moving by signature is the commercial face of obtaining.
senses.whyCN: 所有权靠签字转移，是「取得」在商业上的面孔。

senses.title: Something obtained
senses.definition: the object or collection that has been bought or added
senses.definitionCN: 被买下或添入的物品或收藏
senses.example: The new acquisition will go on display in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 新入藏的这件作品将在春天展出。
senses.why: Once the process is over, the noun names what is left in the store room.
senses.whyCN: 过程结束后，这个名词就指库房里留下的那件东西。

senses.title: The learning of a skill or language
senses.definition: the gradual taking in of a language or skill without formal teaching
senses.definitionCN: 不经正式教学而逐渐掌握语言或技能
senses.example: Language acquisition begins long before a child speaks.
senses.exampleCN: 语言习得在孩子开口之前很久就开始了。
senses.why: What is learned is owned as quietly as what is bought loudly.
senses.whyCN: 学到的东西被拥有得悄无声息，正如买来的东西来得声势浩大。

intro.en: Acquisition is the noun of acquire, and it names both the act and the thing that changes hands.
intro.cn: acquisition 是 acquire 的名词，既指动作，也指易手的那件东西。

items.en: The verb meant to seek.
items.cn: 那个动词意为「寻找」。

items.en: Acquisitio named the getting of something.
items.cn: acquisitio 指「取得某物」。

items.en: French carried the noun into legal and commercial use.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入法律与商业用途。

items.en: English used it first for property and rights.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指财产与权利。

items.en: Business gave it the takeover sense, and linguistics gave it the sense of learning.
items.cn: 商业赋予它「收购」义，语言学赋予它「习得」义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acquire family; the near-meaning group is words for purchases and takeovers.
note.cn: 形近组是 acquire 词族；近义组是表示购入与接管的词。

entries.definition: To obtain or buy something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得；收购」，是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: Keen to acquire possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「贪得的」。

entries.definition: Gained after birth rather than inherited.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「后天获得的」。

entries.definition: The act of buying something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「购买」，最贴近的日常对应词。

entries.definition: The act of gaining control of a company.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接管」，侧重控制权。

entries.definition: The obtaining of supplies, especially for an organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「采购」，多指机构的物资获取。

entries.definition: The reaching of a skill or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「达到、造诣」，多指技能水平。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the merger phrase and the museum store room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用并购这个固定说法，以及博物馆库房的画面。

normal.en: Acquire plus ition: the act of getting, and the thing got.
normal.cn: acquire 加 ition：取得这个动作，以及取得的那件东西。

normal.en: Mergers and acquisitions is the fixed business phrase; the plural is almost always used.
normal.cn: mergers and acquisitions 是固定商业说法，几乎总用复数。

normal.en: Language acquisition is the linguists' term for learning a first language.
normal.cn: language acquisition 是语言学家指母语习得的术语。

normal.en: A museum's new acquisition is the object, not the purchase.
normal.cn: 博物馆的 new acquisition 指那件藏品，而不是那笔购买。

normal.en: Do not use acquisition for a single cheap purchase; it suggests scale.
normal.cn: 不要用 acquisition 指一次便宜的小购买；这个词暗示规模。

abstract.en: Two documents squared on a desk, one key passing between hands.
abstract.cn: 两份文件在桌上对齐，一把钥匙在两手之间传递。

abstract.en: A crate opened in a store room, the label still fresh.
abstract.cn: 库房里打开的木箱，标签还很新。

abstract.en: A child hearing a word once and owning it for life.
abstract.cn: 孩子听到一个词一次，就一辈子拥有它。

examples.en: The acquisition of the painting was funded by private donors.
examples.cn: 这幅画的购藏由私人捐赠者出资。

examples.en: The company announced the acquisition of a rival chain.
examples.cn: 公司宣布收购一家竞争连锁店。

examples.en: Second language acquisition depends heavily on exposure.
examples.cn: 第二语言习得在很大程度上依赖接触。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额快贼神」——额头上贴着「快贼神」的清单，列着要买下的一切

root: 源自拉丁语 acquisitio「取得」，出自动词 acquirere（ad- 朝向 + quaerere 寻找）；经古法语 acquisition 进入英语，十五世纪起用于财产与权利，后扩展出并购与语言习得义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses name a process and its leftovers: the act of obtaining, a company taken over, the object added, and a language absorbed.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项命名一个过程及其剩余物：取得这一动作、被接管的公司、添入的物件，以及被吸收进头脑的语言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key moving from one hand to another over a signed page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把钥匙在一页签好的纸上从一只手移到另一只手。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: getting something, described as a course of events.
branches.cn: 过程线：把取得某物描述为一段经过。

branches.en: THE FIRM: control passes with a signature.
branches.cn: 企业线：控制权随签字转移。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: what arrives in the store room.
branches.cn: 物件线：运进库房的那件东西。

branches.en: THE MIND: a language is taken in without a receipt.
branches.cn: 心智线：语言被收进头脑，却没有收据。

branches.en: THE PAIR: every acquisition leaves both an act and an object.
branches.cn: 成对线：每一次取得，都留下一个动作与一件东西。

intro.en: A Latin verb of seeking, a Latin noun of getting, and an English ending carry the word.
intro.cn: 一个寻找动词、一个取得名词加一个英语词尾，撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin acquisitio is attested and passes through French; English records the noun from the fifteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acquisitio 有文献可证，经法语传入；英语自十五世纪起记录这个名词。

items.example: It marks the direction of the getting.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「取得」的方向。

items.example: It is the search inside the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个名词内部的寻找。

items.example: It turns the verb into this noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成这个名词。

items.example: It forms acquisitions.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquisitions。

items.example: It forms acquisitive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquisitive。

items.example: It forms acquired.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acquired。

items.example: It pairs with acquisition in business writing.
items.exampleCN: 它在商业写作中与 acquisition 并列。

items.example: It is the everyday word for a hostile acquisition.
items.exampleCN: 它是「敌意收购」的日常说法。

definition_zh: 英亩；土地；田地；大片
definition_en: a unit of land area, or a piece of land measured in such units
core_image: 一头牛拉着犁，一个上午刚好犁完的那一小片地
scene: 老农用手杖在地上划出一块方地，说这块地够一家人种一季麦子。The old farmer marked a square of ground with his stick and said that one acre there would feed a family for a season.
sceneCN: 这里 acre 指一块以英亩计量的土地（第 1 个义项：面积单位）；句意为老农用手杖划出一块方地，说这一英亩够一家人种一季麦子。

derivatives.zh: 由 acre 加 -age 构成，义为「土地面积；英亩数」
由 acre 与 foot 复合而成，义为「英亩英尺」，一种水量单位

senses.title: A unit of land area
senses.definition: a measure of land equal to about four thousand square metres
senses.definitionCN: 一种土地面积单位，约合四千平方米
senses.example: One acre is roughly the size of a football pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 一英亩大约相当于一个足球场大小。
senses.why: The Old English word meant a field, and the measure grew out of how much a pair of oxen could plough in a day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里这个词意为「田地」，这个单位来自一对牛一天能犁完的地。

senses.title: A piece of land
senses.definition: a plot or expanse of ground, often farmland, counted in acres
senses.definitionCN: 一块或一片土地，多为农田，以英亩计数
senses.example: They keep a few acres behind the house for horses.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后留了几英亩地养马。
senses.why: The measure became a way of naming the ground itself, especially in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位后来变成对土地本身的称呼，尤其在复数里。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: in the plural, a great extent of something, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 用复数时指某物的一大片，多为比喻用法
senses.example: The new estate covers acres of concrete and glass.
senses.exampleCN: 新园区铺开大片混凝土与玻璃。
senses.why: Land is the original measure of bigness, so acres came to mean plenty of anything.
senses.whyCN: 土地原本就是「大」的尺度，于是 acres 用来表示任何东西的一大片。

intro.en: Acre is one of the oldest land words in English, older than the measure it now names.
intro.cn: acre 是英语里最古老的土地词之一，比它今天所指的单位更老。

items.en: A reconstructed root agro- meant a field or open land.
items.cn: 重构词根 agro- 意为「田地、开阔地」。

items.en: Æcer meant a field, an enclosed piece of farmland.
items.cn: æcer 意为「田地」，一块圈起来的农田。

items.en: The Germanic form meant an open cultivated field.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式意为「开阔的耕地」。

items.en: The word appears in early charters as a unit of ploughland.
items.cn: 这个词在早期地契里作为耕地单位出现。

items.en: The acre was fixed by statute, and the word now also means a large expanse.
items.cn: 英亩由法令固定下来，这个词现在也指一大片。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acre family; the near-meaning group is land measures and land words.
note.cn: 形近组是 acre 词族；近义组是土地计量与土地词。

entries.definition: An area of land measured in acres.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「土地面积；英亩数」。

entries.definition: The volume of one acre covered to a depth of one foot.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「英亩英尺」，一英亩面积上一英尺深的水量。

entries.definition: The Latin word for field, a cousin of acre.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，拉丁语里的「田地」，与本词同源。

entries.definition: A metric unit of land area, about two and a half acres.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公顷」，约合二点五英亩。

entries.definition: A small measured piece of land.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小块地」，面积通常很小。

entries.definition: An area of open land used for crops or animals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「田地」，指耕作的开放地面。

entries.definition: A large area of land owned by one person or family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「庄园、地产」，强调大片与归属。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the ploughland origin and the plural, which names land itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用「一牛一犁之地」的来历，以及指土地本身的复数形式。

normal.en: An acre began as the land a team of oxen could plough in a day.
normal.cn: 一英亩最初是一队牛一天能犁完的地。

normal.en: The plural acres often means land rather than a number of units.
normal.cn: 复数 acres 常指土地本身，而不是若干单位。

normal.en: Acreage is the derived noun for the total area of a farm.
normal.cn: acreage 是派生名词，指一块地的总英亩数。

normal.en: A hectare is about two and a half acres, the metric neighbour.
normal.cn: 一公顷约合二点五英亩，是公制的邻居。

normal.en: Acres of something means a great deal of it, usually open and spreading.
normal.cn: acres of 某物意为大量的某物，通常有铺展开来的感觉。

abstract.en: An ox walking a slow circle while the plough turns dark soil.
abstract.cn: 一头牛绕着慢圈走，犁把土翻成深色。

abstract.en: A square marked out with a stick in a field of grass.
abstract.cn: 草地上用一根手杖划出的方块。

abstract.en: Fence posts marching away until the eye cannot follow.
abstract.cn: 栅栏柱一路排开，直到眼睛跟不上。

examples.en: One acre of well-watered soil can feed a large family.
examples.cn: 一英亩水浇得好的地能养活一大家人。

examples.en: The orchard occupies an acre behind the barn.
examples.cn: 果园占了谷仓后面一英亩地。

examples.en: Land prices here are quoted per acre.
examples.cn: 这里的土地价格按每英亩报价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克」——一克土太少，一英亩才够种地

root: 古英语 æcer「田地」直接继承日耳曼语 akraz，可上溯重构词根 agro-「田地」；拉丁语同源词为 ager，故 acre 既是面积单位，也保留「田地」这一最古老的意思。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses grow from one field: a fixed measure, the ground counted by that measure, and the figurative plenty of acres.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从一块田里长出来：固定的单位、按此单位计数的土地，以及比喻意义上的「大片」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the ground one ox team could turn in a morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队牛在一个上午里翻完的地。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a day's ploughing became a fixed unit.
branches.cn: 单位线：一天的犁地变成一个固定单位。

branches.en: THE GROUND: the unit turned back into land itself.
branches.cn: 土地线：单位又转回来指土地本身。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: acres of anything means an open, spreading plenty.
branches.cn: 比喻线：acres of 某物意为铺展开的大片。

branches.en: THE FIELD: measure and ground are two faces of the same plot.
branches.cn: 田地线：单位与土地，是同一块地的两面。

branches.en: THE OPENNESS: land and largeness share the same horizon.
branches.cn: 开阔线：土地与广大共用同一条地平线。

intro.en: One ancient root for field survives in the measure, the land word and the Latin cousin.
intro.cn: 一个意为「田地」的古老词根，留在单位、土地词与拉丁同源词里。

latinIntro.en: Old English æcer and Latin ager are cognates from a shared Indo-European root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 æcer 与拉丁语 ager 同出一个印欧词根，是姊妹词。

items.example: It is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的基座。

items.example: It is the direct ancestor of acre.
items.exampleCN: 它是 acre 的直接祖先。

items.example: It is the reconstructed Indo-European source.
items.exampleCN: 它是重构的印欧语源头。

items.example: It is the Latin cousin of acre.
items.exampleCN: 它是 acre 的拉丁姊妹词。

items.example: It forms acreage.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acreage。

items.example: It forms acres, often meaning land.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acres，常指土地。

items.example: It comes from the same Latin field word.
items.exampleCN: 它出自同一个表示「田地」的拉丁词。

items.example: Its first element is the Latin field word.
items.exampleCN: 它的前一部分就是那个拉丁语「田地」词。

definition_zh: 横过；穿过；在对面；遍及；传达
definition_en: from one side of something to the other, or on the opposite side
core_image: 一条线从左岸拉到右岸，中间没有断开
scene: 孩子们把绳子系在两棵树之间，然后一个接一个走过去。The children tied a rope between two trees and then walked across it one by one.
sceneCN: 这里 across 指从绳子的一边走到另一边（第 1 个义项：横过）；句意为孩子们在两棵树间系绳，然后逐个走过去。

derivatives.zh: 与 across 同源的 base 词，义为「十字；穿过」
由 cross 加 -ing 构成，义为「穿越；十字路口」

senses.title: From one side to the other
senses.definition: moving or extending from one side of something to the opposite side
senses.definitionCN: 从某物的一边移动或延伸到另一边
senses.example: The bridge runs across the river at its narrowest point.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥在河面最窄处横跨过去。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning in the form of a cross, and a cross is a line that goes from side to side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是个短语，意为「成十字形」，而十字正是一条从一边到另一边的线。

senses.title: On the opposite side
senses.definition: positioned on the other side of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的另一边
senses.example: The pharmacy is across the street from the school.
senses.exampleCN: 药房在学校对面的街上。
senses.why: Once the line has been crossed, the far end of it becomes a place to stand.
senses.whyCN: 线一旦被跨过，它的另一端就成了可以站立的地方。

senses.title: Throughout an area
senses.definition: spread over the whole of a region or group
senses.definitionCN: 铺展在整个地区或群体之上
senses.example: The story spread across the country within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事一周内传遍全国。
senses.why: A line drawn side to side also reaches every point between the edges.
senses.whyCN: 一条从一边画到另一边的线，也覆盖了两端之间的每一点。

senses.title: So as to be understood
senses.definition: in phrases such as get across, to make an idea reach other people
senses.definitionCN: 用于 get across 一类短语，指让想法抵达别人
senses.example: The teacher used a diagram to get the idea across.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用一张图把这个想法讲清楚。
senses.why: Understanding is treated as a distance, and getting across is reaching the far bank.
senses.whyCN: 理解被当作一段距离，讲清楚就是抵达对岸。

senses.title: To meet by chance
senses.definition: in the phrase come across, to find or meet something without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 用于 come across，指没有刻意寻找而遇到或发现
senses.example: I came across an old photograph in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 我在抽屉里偶然发现一张旧照片。
senses.why: Walking across a space is how one happens to run into what lies there.
senses.whyCN: 走过一片地方，正是会碰上那里东西的方式。

intro.en: Across began as a phrase about the shape of a cross, and it still draws a line from side to side.
intro.cn: across 最初是一个关于十字形状的短语，至今仍在画一条从一边到另一边的线。

items.en: Crux meant a cross, an instrument of crossing lines.
items.cn: crux 意为「十字」，两条线相交的形状。

items.en: French crois meant a cross.
items.cn: 法语 crois 意为「十字」。

items.en: The phrase a crois meant in the form of a cross, hence crossing over.
items.cn: 短语 a crois 意为「成十字形」，因而有「横越」之意。

items.en: The phrase fused into the single word across.
items.cn: 这个短语合成了一个单词 across。

items.en: The word added figurative uses such as get across and come across.
items.cn: 这个词又添上 get across 与 come across 等比喻用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the cross family; the near-meaning group is prepositions of passage.
note.cn: 形近组是 cross 词族；近义组是表示穿越的介词。

entries.definition: To go from one side to the other, or a mark of two lines.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「穿过」或「十字」，是 across 的词干。

entries.definition: A place or act of going across.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「穿越；路口」。

entries.definition: In a direction that crosses something else.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「横向地」。

entries.definition: Above and to the other side of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「越过、在……上方」，常可与 across 互换。

entries.definition: From one end or side to the other, inside something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「穿过」，强调在内部通过。

entries.definition: On the farther side of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……那一边」，强调远端。

entries.definition: From side to side of something; a literary synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「横过」，古雅或文学用法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the cross shape and the fixed phrases the word lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用十字的形状，以及这个词固定的几个短语。

normal.en: Across comes from a phrase meaning in the shape of a cross.
normal.cn: across 出自一个意为「成十字形」的短语。

normal.en: Get across means make an idea reach the other side of a mind.
normal.cn: get across 意为让想法抵达对方头脑的另一边。

normal.en: Come across means meet by accident while moving along.
normal.cn: come across 意为在走动时偶然碰上。

normal.en: Across from is the phrase for facing something on the other side.
normal.cn: across from 指隔着某物相对。

normal.en: Across is a preposition or adverb, not a verb; the verb is cross.
normal.cn: across 是介词或副词，不是动词；动词是 cross。

abstract.en: A rope stretched between two trees, a child stepping onto it.
abstract.cn: 两棵树间拉起的绳子，一个孩子踩上去。

abstract.en: A line drawn through a map from border to border.
abstract.cn: 在地图上从边界画到边界的一条线。

abstract.en: A word spoken on one bank and understood on the other.
abstract.cn: 一岸说出的话，在另一岸被听懂。

examples.en: We walked across the field to reach the farmhouse.
examples.cn: 我们穿过田野走到农舍。

examples.en: The bakery is across from the post office.
examples.cn: 面包店在邮局对面。

examples.en: She could not get her point across to the committee.
examples.cn: 她没能让委员会明白她的观点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额克罗斯」——额头上画个十字，从这一横走到那一横

root: 由中古英语短语 a crois「成十字形」融合而成，源自古法语 crois、拉丁语 crux「十字」；十字是横贯的线，故引申为「横过、在对面、遍及」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all draw one line from side to side: a crossing, the far bank, the whole width, an idea reaching a listener, and a chance meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都在画同一条从一边到另一边的线：横越、对岸、整幅宽度、抵达听者的想法，以及偶然的相遇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one unbroken line from the left bank to the right.
core.cn: 核心意象：从左岸到右岸一条不断的线。

branches.en: THE PASSAGE: body or line moves side to side.
branches.cn: 穿越线：身体或线条从一边走到另一边。

branches.en: THE FAR BANK: the other end becomes a place to stand.
branches.cn: 对岸线：另一端成了可以站立的地方。

branches.en: THE WIDTH: the line covers everything between its ends.
branches.cn: 宽度线：线覆盖了两端之间的一切。

branches.en: THE MIND: an idea crosses the gap to a listener.
branches.cn: 心智线：想法跨过空隙抵达听者。

branches.en: THE CHANCE: walking along is how one runs into things.
branches.cn: 偶然线：沿着走，正是碰上东西的方式。

intro.en: The word is a fused French phrase about a cross, and its family is built on cross.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个关于十字的法语短语融合而成，词族建在 cross 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin crux and French crois are attested; the English word appears in the fourteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crux 与法语 crois 均有文献可证；英语这个词出现于十四世纪。

items.example: It survives in the phrase a crois.
items.exampleCN: 它留在 a crois 这个短语里。

items.example: It is the visible core of across.
items.exampleCN: 它是 across 里看得见的核心。

items.example: It is the Latin source of the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个形象来自这个拉丁名词。

items.example: It passed the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词传给英语。

items.example: It forms crossing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 crossing。

items.meaning: in the manner or direction of
items.example: It forms crosswise.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 crosswise。

items.example: It is the nearest everyday neighbour.
items.exampleCN: 它是日常最接近的邻词。

items.example: It differs by insisting on the inside.
items.exampleCN: 它的不同在于强调内部。

latinEntries.meaning: to torment, originally to put on a cross

derivatives.zh: 与 across 同源的 base 词，义为「十字；穿过」
由 cross 加 -ing 构成，义为「穿越；十字路口」

definition_zh: 行动；行为；表演；起作用；法案；一幕
definition_en: to do something; to perform a role; to have an effect; a deed or a law; a division of a play
core_image: 一个人把手从袖子里伸出来，真的做成了一件事
scene: 舞台灯亮起时，她其实一点也不生气，却要让台下所有人都相信。On stage she had to act anger that she did not feel at all.
sceneCN: 这里 act 指用表演呈现某种情绪（第 2 个义项：表演）；句意为她在舞台上必须演出自己并未感到的愤怒。

derivatives.zh: 由 act 加 -ion 构成，义为「行动；举动」
由 act 加 -or 构成，义为「演员」
由 en- 加 act 构成，义为「颁布；制定法律」

senses.title: Something done
senses.definition: a single thing that a person does, especially one with meaning or effect
senses.definitionCN: 人所做的一件具体的事，尤指有意义或有效果的举动
senses.example: Their first act was to open every window in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们做的第一件事是把房子里所有的窗户都打开。
senses.why: The Latin root simply means to do, so an act is a doing that can be pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义就是「做」，所以 act 指一件能被指认出来的「做过的事」。

senses.title: To perform a role
senses.definition: to perform a part in a play, film or show
senses.definitionCN: 在戏剧、电影或演出中扮演某个角色
senses.example: He acted Hamlet for the first time at twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 他二十岁时第一次扮演哈姆雷特。
senses.why: On stage a deed is repeated at fixed times, so the verb of doing also covers performing.
senses.whyCN: 舞台上的「做」要按固定时刻重复，于是这个表示「做」的动词也用来指表演。

senses.title: To have an effect
senses.definition: to produce an effect on something; to work as a force
senses.definitionCN: 对某物产生影响；作为一种力量发生作用
senses.example: The acid acts on the metal within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酸几秒钟内就作用于金属。
senses.why: A force that changes matter is doing something to it, and English keeps the plain verb of doing.
senses.whyCN: 改变物质的力量是在对它「做事」，英语就沿用了那个最朴素的「做」。

senses.title: A law passed by a parliament
senses.definition: a formal law made by a legislature
senses.definitionCN: 由立法机构正式通过的法律
senses.example: The act limits fishing in the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案限制在海湾捕鱼。
senses.why: A statute is a deed done collectively and written down, so the result of doing became a document.
senses.whyCN: 法律是集体「做」下的事被写入文本，于是「做」的结果变成了一份文书。

senses.title: A division of a play
senses.definition: one of the main sections into which a play is divided
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧作品被划分出的主要段落之一
senses.example: The second act ends with a long silence.
senses.exampleCN: 第二幕以一段长久的沉默结束。
senses.why: Each stage section is one completed stretch of acting, and the noun took its name from that.
senses.whyCN: 舞台上每一段都是一个完整的「演」，名词「一幕」正是由此得名。

intro.en: Act goes back to a Latin verb for doing and driving, and its senses spread from deeds to stages and statute books.
intro.cn: act 可追溯到表示「做」与「驱动」的拉丁动词，词义从行为一路铺到舞台与法典。

items.en: Agere meant to do, to drive, to set something in motion.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使某物动起来」。

items.en: Its participle actus named a doing or a driving, and supplied the stem act-.
items.cn: 它的分词 actus 表示「一次做、一次驱动」，并提供了 act- 这个词干。

items.en: In legal language an actum was a deed formally recorded.
items.cn: 在法律用语里，actum 指正式记录在案的行为。

items.en: French used acte both for a deed and for a section of a play.
items.cn: 法语用 acte 兼指「行为」与戏剧中的「一幕」。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French, first for deeds and stage sections.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入这个词，最初用于行为与戏剧段落。

items.en: The legal sense widened to any statute, and the verb kept the sense of doing and performing.
items.cn: 法律义扩展为任何成文法案，动词则保留了「做」与「表演」两义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the family built on the same root; the near-meaning group is the verbs and nouns of doing.
note.cn: 形近组是同根词族；近义组是表示「做」的动词与名词。

entries.definition: The process or thing of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动；举动」。

entries.definition: A person who performs on stage or screen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演员」。

entries.definition: To make a proposal into law.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「颁布、制定为法律」。

entries.definition: To do things in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「举止、表现」，强调方式。

entries.definition: To carry out a task or play a role before an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执行；演出」。

entries.definition: A notable thing that someone does.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事迹、行为」，多指值得称道之事。

entries.definition: A written law passed by a legislature.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成文法、法令」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks run from the plain verb of doing to its stage and legal branches.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从最朴素的「做」出发，走到舞台与法律两条分支。

normal.en: The root means to do, so act is the shortest possible word for a deed.
normal.cn: 词根本义是「做」，所以 act 是表示行为的最短的一个词。

normal.en: Act on a plan means to carry it out; act as a chair means to serve as one.
normal.cn: act on a plan 是把计划执行下去；act as a chair 是充当一把椅子。

normal.en: On stage, act is both the verb to perform and the noun for a section of the play.
normal.cn: 在舞台上，act 既是「扮演」的动词，也是「一幕」的名词。

normal.en: A parliament enacts a bill, and the finished text is then called an act.
normal.cn: 议会 enact 一项议案，定稿后的文本便称作 an act。

normal.en: Do not confuse act with action: act points at one deed, action at a course of doing.
normal.cn: 别把 act 与 action 混用：act 指一件事，action 指一段行动过程。

abstract.en: A hand leaving a sleeve and actually finishing the thing.
abstract.cn: 一只手离开袖子，把事情真正做完。

abstract.en: A curtain lifting on a stage where someone else's anger is worn like a coat.
abstract.cn: 幕布升起，别人生的怒气被像外套一样穿上。

abstract.en: A printed page of law, every line a deed frozen in ink.
abstract.cn: 一页印好的法律，每一行都是被墨固定下来的行为。

examples.en: He had to act calm while the alarm was still ringing.
examples.cn: 警报还在响的时候，他不得不装出一副镇定的样子。

examples.en: Parliament passed an act banning single-use plastics.
examples.cn: 议会通过了一项禁止一次性塑料制品的法案。

examples.en: These chemicals act on the nervous system within minutes.
examples.cn: 这些化学物质几分钟内就作用于神经系统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克特」——阿克克制住手抖，把这一幕演到底

root: 源自拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」，其分词 actus 提供词干 act-；经古法语 acte 于十四世纪进入英语，先指行为与戏剧段落，后扩展出「法案」义；同根词有 action、actor、enact 与 agenda。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all grow from one Latin verb meaning to do: a deed, a role, a force at work, a written law, and a section of a play.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都出自同一个意为「做」的拉丁动词：一件行为、一个角色、一股作用力、一部成文法，以及戏台上的一幕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that actually finishes the thing it reaches for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手真正把伸手要够的东西做成了。

branches.en: THE DEED: the plainest kind of doing, one countable thing.
branches.cn: 行为线：最朴素的「做」，一件可以数出来的事。

branches.en: THE STAGE: the same doing repeated on cue before an audience.
branches.cn: 舞台线：同样的「做」在观众面前按提示重复。

branches.en: THE FORCE: doing without a body, as acid does to metal.
branches.cn: 力量线：没有身体的「做」，如酸作用于金属。

branches.en: THE STATUTE: a deed done by many and written into law.
branches.cn: 法案线：许多人共同做下的事，被写进法律。

branches.en: THE PLAY: a play cut into stretches of acting.
branches.cn: 戏剧线：一部戏被切分成几段「演」。

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing, a Latin participle, and a set of English endings built act and its family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的拉丁动词、一个拉丁分词，加上一组英语词尾，造出了 act 及其词族。

latinIntro.en: Agere and its participle actus are well attested in Latin; English records act from the fourteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: agere 及其分词 actus 在拉丁语中均有文献可证；英语自十四世纪起记录 act。

items.example: It is the base of act, agent and agenda.
items.exampleCN: 它是 act、agent 与 agenda 的共同基础。

items.example: It gives the stem act- that English keeps.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了英语保留的词干 act-。

items.example: It is both noun and verb in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语中既是名词也是动词。

items.example: It forms actor.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actor。

items.example: It forms action.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 action。

items.example: It forms enact, to put a bill into law.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 enact，即把议案变成法律。

items.example: It forms acting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acting。

items.example: It forms acted.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acted。

items.example: It forms acts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acts。

items.example: It forms actress.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actress。

derivatives.zh: 由 act 加 -ion 构成，义为「行动；举动」
由 act 加 -or 构成，义为「演员」

definition_zh: 启动；激活；使活跃起来
definition_en: to switch something on; to make a substance or function start working; to stir people into action
core_image: 一只手指按下开关，原本静止的机器开始转动
scene: 地下车库的灯平时不亮，只有人走近时才会自动通电。In the underground car park the lights stay off until a sensor activates them.
sceneCN: 这里 activates 指让设备通电开始工作（第 1 个义项：启动）；句意为地下车库的灯在人走近时由传感器启动。

derivatives.zh: 由 activate 加 -ion 构成，义为「启动；激活」
由 activate 加 -or 构成，义为「活化剂；启动装置」
由 de- 加 activate 构成，义为「停用；关闭」

senses.title: To switch a device into operation
senses.definition: to make a machine or system begin to work
senses.definitionCN: 使机器或系统开始运转
senses.example: The sensor activates the light when a car comes near.
senses.exampleCN: 有车靠近时，传感器就会启动这盏灯。
senses.why: The ending -ate turns a state into an action, so act becomes the act of setting something to work.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ate 把状态变成动作，于是「做」变成了「让某物开始做」。

senses.title: To make a substance or function start working
senses.definition: to set a chemical, gene or body function going
senses.definitionCN: 使某种化学物质、基因或身体功能开始发挥作用
senses.example: Enzymes activate the protein once it reaches the gut.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质一到肠道，酶就把它激活。
senses.why: Science needed a word for switching a dormant thing on, and the plain verb of doing was ready.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个词表示「把休眠之物打开」，而那个朴素的「做」正好可用。

senses.title: To stir people into action
senses.definition: to make a person or group begin doing something
senses.definitionCN: 使某个人或群体开始行动起来
senses.example: The campaign activated thousands of young voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动动员了数千名年轻选民。
senses.why: People who were passive begin to do, and they are switched on much as a machine is.
senses.whyCN: 本来被动的人开始做事，他们被打开的方式和机器几乎一样。

intro.en: Activate is English act fitted with a Latin ending that means to make, so it names the moment a dormant thing starts doing.
intro.cn: activate 是英语 act 加上一个意为「使」的拉丁词尾，命名的是休眠之物开始「做」的那一刻。

items.en: Agere meant to do and to drive, and gave Latin its word for action.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动」，为拉丁语提供了「行动」一词。

items.en: Its participle actus, a doing, supplied the stem act- to later languages.
items.cn: 它的分词 actus 表示「一次做」，为后来的语言提供了词干 act-。

items.en: English took act for a deed and for performing, and used it as noun and verb.
items.cn: 英语以 act 表示行为与表演，名词动词两用。

items.en: The ending -atus marked something made or provided with a quality.
items.cn: 词尾 -atus 表示「被造成」或「被赋予某种性质」。

items.en: English verbs in -ate name the act of putting something into that state.
items.cn: 英语中带 -ate 的动词表示「使某物进入那种状态」。

items.en: Technology and biology took activate up for switching devices and chemicals on.
items.cn: 技术与生物学接手 activate，用它表示把设备与化学物质「打开」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the act- stem; the near-meaning group is the verbs of setting things going.
note.cn: 形近组共享 act- 词干；近义组是表示「使某事开始」的动词。

entries.definition: Busy doing things, or producing an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活跃的；起作用的」。

entries.definition: The act of switching something on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「启动；激活」。

entries.definition: To switch something off or make it inactive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停用；关闭」。

entries.definition: To begin operating or to cause to begin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开始；发动」，最通用。

entries.definition: To set off a reaction or event suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「触发」，强调突然引起。

entries.definition: To make something possible or usable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使可用；使能够」。

entries.definition: To turn a device on by a switch.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「打开开关」，最口语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the switch: a device, a chemical, and a crowd of people all start doing at once.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都围着那个开关转：设备、化学物质、一群人，同时开始「做」。

normal.en: Act plus -ate means to put into doing, which is exactly what a switch does.
normal.cn: act 加 -ate 意为「使进入做的状态」，开关做的正是这件事。

normal.en: Phones, alarms and accounts are all activated before they can be used.
normal.cn: 手机、警报与账户都要先 activate 才能使用。

normal.en: In biology an enzyme activates a protein; the protein was there but idle.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，酶 activate 一种蛋白质；那蛋白质本来就在，只是闲着。

normal.en: Activate people means to rouse them from passivity into doing.
normal.cn: activate people 是把人从被动状态唤起来做事。

normal.en: The opposite is deactivate, the prefix de- undoing what was switched on.
normal.cn: 反义是 deactivate，前缀 de- 撤掉先前打开的状态。

abstract.en: A finger pressing a switch and a whole silent room coming awake.
abstract.cn: 一根手指按下开关，整个安静的房间醒了过来。

abstract.en: A sleeping enzyme opening one eye at the touch of the right molecule.
abstract.cn: 沉睡的酶在遇到对的分子时睁开一只眼。

abstract.en: A crowd that was merely standing there suddenly all begin to move.
abstract.cn: 原本只是站着的人群，忽然全都动了起来。

examples.en: Press the red button to activate the alarm.
examples.cn: 按下红色按钮即可启动警报。

examples.en: Sunlight can activate the compound in the glass.
examples.cn: 阳光可以激活玻璃中的那种化合物。

examples.en: A good coach knows how to activate a tired team.
examples.cn: 好教练懂得怎样把一支疲惫的队伍重新带动起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提维特」——阿克一按开关，整条生产线都动起来

root: 由英语 act 加拉丁语词尾 -atus（英语作 -ate，表示「使……进入某状态」）构成；act 源自拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」，分词 actus 提供词干 act-；该词在近现代科技语境中定型，用于启动设备、激活物质或动员人群。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one move, switching something from idle to doing: a device, a substance, and a group of people.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用同一个动作——把某物从闲置切换到「做」：一台设备、一种物质、一群人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger on a switch, and the still machine begins to turn.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指按在开关上，静止的机器开始转动。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: current flows and the machine works again.
branches.cn: 设备线：电流一通，机器重新工作。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: a sleeping chemical is woken by the right trigger.
branches.cn: 物质线：沉睡的化学物质被对的触发物唤醒。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: passive onlookers are roused into doing.
branches.cn: 人群线：被动的旁观者被唤起而行动。

branches.en: THE SENSOR: the switch may be thrown by a machine rather than a hand.
branches.cn: 传感器线：按下开关的也可能是机器而非人手。

branches.en: THE CHAIN: one activation often sets off the next step.
branches.cn: 连锁线：一次激活常常点燃下一步。

intro.en: The root act- carries the idea of doing, and the suffix -ate adds the idea of making something enter that state.
intro.cn: 词干 act- 承载「做」的意思，后缀 -ate 再加上「使某物进入该状态」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere and actus are attested, and the ending -atus regularly became English -ate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere 与 actus 均有文献可证，词尾 -atus 常规律地变为英语 -ate。

definition_zh: 活跃的；积极的；起作用的；活的（火山）；主动的
definition_en: busy and doing things; producing an effect; still able to erupt; of the active voice
core_image: 一个不停在动的人，手边总有一件正在做的事
scene: 社区里那位七十岁的老人每天骑车送报，还带头组织周末的河岸清理。At seventy the neighbour is still active, cycling to deliver papers and leading weekend clean-ups.
sceneCN: 这里 active 指人精力充沛、一直在做事（第 1 个义项：活跃的）；句意为这位七十岁的邻居仍然活跃，骑车送报并带头做周末清理。

pos.zh: 活跃的；积极的；起作用的；活的（火山）；主动的

senses.title: Busy and doing things
senses.definition: often doing things; full of energy and movement
senses.definitionCN: 经常做事、充满精力与活动的
senses.example: She remains active in local politics.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍然活跃于本地政界。
senses.why: The Latin adjective describes what is doing, not merely what is able to do.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词形容「正在做」的东西，而不只是「能做」的东西。

senses.title: Producing an effect
senses.definition: of a substance or factor, having a real effect
senses.definitionCN: 指某物质或因素真正产生效果
senses.example: The active ingredient is aspirin.
senses.exampleCN: 有效成分是阿司匹林。
senses.why: In a mixture the one part that acts is the part that earns the word.
senses.whyCN: 在混合物里，真正「起作用」的那一部分才配得上这个词。

senses.title: Of a volcano, still erupting
senses.definition: of a volcano, still able to erupt
senses.definitionCN: 指火山仍然可能喷发
senses.example: The mountain beyond the town is an active volcano.
senses.exampleCN: 镇子外那座山是一座活火山。
senses.why: Geology borrowed the word for what is still doing something, even if only slowly.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用了这个词，指仍在「做事」的东西，哪怕动作很慢。

senses.title: Of the active voice
senses.definition: of a verb form in which the subject performs the action
senses.definitionCN: 指主语执行动作的动词形式
senses.example: The sentence is written in the active voice.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子用的是主动语态。
senses.why: Grammar names the voice where the subject acts, keeping the verb of doing in plain view.
senses.whyCN: 语法把主语「做」事的那种语态命名为主动，始终让那个表示「做」的动词留在明面上。

intro.en: Active is the Latin adjective of doing carried into English through French, then stretched to grammar and geology.
intro.cn: active 是拉丁语中表示「做」的形容词，经法语进入英语，之后又被语法与地质学各借去一用。

items.en: Agere meant to do and to drive, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动」，是整个词族的根。

items.en: Its participle actus, a doing, gave the stem from which the adjective was made.
items.cn: 它的分词 actus 表示「一次做」，提供了造出这个形容词的词干。

items.en: Activus described a thing disposed to act or already at work.
items.cn: activus 形容某物倾向于行动或已经处在活动中。

items.en: French carried the adjective for busy persons and working substances.
items.cn: 法语用这个形容词指忙碌的人与正在起作用的物质。

items.en: English adopted it, at first for people and later for medicines and forces.
items.cn: 英语采纳了它，先用于人，后来用于药物与力量。

items.en: Grammar took active for a voice, and geology took it for a volcano still able to erupt.
items.cn: 语法借它命名一种语态，地质学借它指仍可能喷发的火山。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same root family; the near-meaning group is the adjectives of energy and business.
note.cn: 形近组是同根词族；近义组是表示有精力、忙碌的形容词。

entries.definition: To do something or perform a role.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行动；表演」。

entries.definition: The doing of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动；举动」。

entries.definition: Something people do, or the state of being busy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「活动；活跃」。

entries.definition: To switch something on.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「启动；激活」。

entries.definition: Full of energy and ready to move.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精力充沛的」。

entries.definition: Full of life and quick in movement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活泼的；有生气的」。

entries.definition: Occupied with many things to do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「忙碌的」，只强调事务多。

entries.definition: Full of change, force and new activity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有活力的；不断变化的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow what is still doing: a person, a medicine, a mountain, and a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都盯着「还在做事」的东西：一个人、一味药、一座山、一个句子。

normal.en: Active is the adjective of act, so it always keeps the idea of doing inside.
normal.cn: active 是 act 的形容词，所以它内部始终保留「做」的意思。

normal.en: An active person does things; a busy person may merely have many things waiting.
normal.cn: active 的人在做事情；busy 的人可能只是有一堆事等着。

normal.en: An active ingredient is the part of a medicine that actually works.
normal.cn: active ingredient 是药物里真正起作用的那个部分。

normal.en: An active volcano is one still able to erupt; a dormant one is only asleep.
normal.cn: active volcano 是仍可能喷发的火山；dormant 只是睡着了。

normal.en: In the active voice the subject does the action: the dog bit the man.
normal.cn: 主动语态里主语执行动作：狗咬了人。

abstract.en: A body that never quite settles into a chair.
abstract.cn: 一副总也坐不安稳的身体。

abstract.en: A white pill that keeps working quietly inside a glass of water.
abstract.cn: 一片白色药片在一杯水里默默起着作用。

abstract.en: A mountain breathing steam, pretending to sleep.
abstract.cn: 一座吐着蒸汽、假装睡着的山。

examples.en: She stays active by walking to work every day.
examples.cn: 她每天走路去上班，以此保持活跃。

examples.en: The cream contains an active ingredient that repairs skin.
examples.cn: 这款面霜含有一种修复皮肤的有效成分。

examples.en: The volcano is still active and vents steam every morning.
examples.cn: 这座火山仍然活跃，每天早晨都会喷出蒸汽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提夫」——阿克提着劲儿，一天到晚不闲着

root: 源自拉丁语 activus「倾向于行动的」，由 agere「做、驱动」的分词词干 act- 加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成；经古法语 actif 于十六世纪进入英语，先指人忙碌，后扩展至药物、火山与语法中的主动语态。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses all describe something at work: an energetic person, an effective substance, a living volcano, and a voice where the subject acts.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都在描述「正在起作用」的东西：精力充沛的人、真正有效的成分、仍然活着的火山，以及主语亲自做事的语态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who is always in the middle of doing something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人总处在某件事的进行当中。

branches.en: THE PERSON: energy shows itself as constant movement.
branches.cn: 人物线：精力表现为不停的活动。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: one part of a mixture is the part that works.
branches.cn: 物质线：混合物里只有一部分真正起作用。

branches.en: THE MOUNTAIN: a slow, dangerous kind of doing under the ground.
branches.cn: 火山线：地底一种缓慢而危险的「做」。

branches.en: THE SENTENCE: the subject is the one who acts.
branches.cn: 句子线：主语就是做事的那一方。

branches.en: THE ROUTINE: activity repeated daily is what keeps a person active.
branches.cn: 日常线：每天重复的活动才让一个人保持活跃。

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing, its participle, and the adjective ending -ivus together make active and its whole family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的拉丁动词、它的分词，加上形容词词尾 -ivus，合起来造出 active 及其整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Agere, actus and activus are all attested in Latin; French actif and English active are recorded from the medieval and early modern periods.
latinIntro.cn: agere、actus、activus 在拉丁语中均有文献可证；法语 actif 与英语 active 分别见于中世纪与近代早期文献。
